rows.translation: 琪琪的电击器滑回手上的金属结构，她轻点眼镜侧面。“莫妮卡？我是琪琪。有个彻底喝醉奶的家伙正往外走。刚才试图摸我。如果她去找乔茜，你们最好别再给她喝了。”她顿了顿。“嗯，不客气。”她放下手，皱眉看着你。“有些人就是喝不了奶。挺可悲的。我刚说到哪了？”
rows.raw: "\n\nKiki’s stunners slide back into the metal on her hand, and she taps the side of her glasses. “Monika? Kiki. Got a real milk-sot heading out. Tried to grope me. Might want to cut her off if she goes for Josie.” She pauses. “Yeah, welcome.” She lowers her hand and frowns at you. “Some people just can’t hold their milk. It’s kind of sad. Where was I?”"

rows.original: She was telling you about how she hooked up the bar so they wouldn’t get caught stealing power and water. But that doesn’t explain how this place looks. Did they build it out of their old spaceship?
rows.translation: 她刚才正说如何连接酒吧设施，避免她们因偷窃水电而被发现。但这解释不了酒吧如今的样子。她们是用旧飞船建造这里的吗？
rows.raw: "\n\nShe was telling you about how she hooked up the bar so they wouldn’t get caught stealing power and water. But that doesn’t explain how this place looks. Did they build it out of their old spaceship?"

rows.original: “Damn right we did,” Kiki says, her low mood disappearing as she grins at you. “When everybody split up, the ship needed a lot more repairs than the four of us could handle. We weren’t sure what to do, but when we found this place, using the ship to make it our new home seemed like the best idea. It was kind of a pain in the ass to get everything down here, though.”
rows.translation: “我们当然这么干了，”琪琪说道，低落情绪一扫而空，朝你咧嘴一笑。“所有人分开后，飞船需要的维修远远超出我们四人的能力。我们不知道该怎么办，可找到这里后，用飞船把它变成新家似乎是最好的主意。不过把所有东西运到下面可真够麻烦。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Damn right we did,” Kiki says, her low mood disappearing as she grins at you. “When everybody split up, the ship needed a lot more repairs than the four of us could handle. We weren’t sure what to do, but when we found this place, using the ship to make it our new home seemed like the best idea. It was kind of a pain in the ass to get everything down here, though.”"

rows.original: You believe it. If the stairway and that narrow hall is the only way in, you can only imagine how long it took to haul everything into the old station. Especially if they had to break down the ship at the spaceport.
rows.translation: 你相信。如果楼梯和那条狭窄走廊是唯一入口，可想而知将一切运进旧车站花了多久。尤其是如果她们还得在太空港拆解飞船。
rows.raw: "\n\nYou believe it. If the stairway and that narrow hall is the only way in, you can only imagine how long it took to haul everything into the old station. Especially if they had to break down the ship at the spaceport."

rows.original: “Eh, yes and no,” Kiki says. “There are scrappers working at the spaceport, and they helped us take the ship apart.” She looks sad for a moment, then continues. “And Karrah and Monika could handle the heavy lifting. Mostly Karrah, but don’t tell Monika I said that. And it’s not like we needed the biggest pieces down here anyway. Selling the engines got us the funds to start this place.”
rows.translation: “呃，对也不全对，”琪琪说道。“太空港有些拆船工，是他们帮我们拆掉飞船。”她神情黯淡片刻，随后继续。“而且卡拉和莫妮卡能负责搬运重物。主要是卡拉，不过别告诉莫妮卡这是我说的。反正我们也不需要把最大零件带到下面。卖掉引擎换来的资金让我们开起了这里。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Eh, yes and no,” Kiki says. “There are scrappers working at the spaceport, and they helped us take the ship apart.” She looks sad for a moment, then continues. “And Karrah and Monika could handle the heavy lifting. Mostly Karrah, but don’t tell Monika I said that. And it’s not like we needed the biggest pieces down here anyway. Selling the engines got us the funds to start this place.”"

rows.original: It was worth it, though. You’ve been to your share of unusual spacer bars during the Planet Rush, but none of them are like this.
rows.translation: 不过这一切很值得。星球淘金潮期间，你去过不少不同寻常的太空人酒吧，却没有一家像这里。
rows.raw: "\n\nIt was worth it, though. You’ve been to your share of unusual spacer bars during the Planet Rush, but none of them are like this."

rows.original: Kiki grins at you again. “Damn right. I knew I couldn’t rebuild the ship’s interior down here, so I tried to make it look as mechanical and armored as possible. We’ve got re-entry rated plating in the hallway, all the old lounge tables in the bar, and I did so much re-rigging on stuff here for hardlight display and sound production that I almost ran out of spare parts.”
rows.translation: 琪琪再次朝你咧嘴一笑。“当然。我知道没法在下面重建飞船内部，所以尽量让这里显得机械化、装甲化。走廊装了能承受重返大气层的装甲板，酒吧使用所有旧休息室桌子；为了硬光显示和声音播放，我改装了太多这里的设备，差点把备用零件用光。”
rows.raw: "\n\nKiki grins at you again. “Damn right. I knew I couldn’t rebuild the ship’s interior down here, so I tried to make it look as mechanical and armored as possible. We’ve got re-entry rated plating in the hallway, all the old lounge tables in the bar, and I did so much re-rigging on stuff here for hardlight display and sound production that I almost ran out of spare parts.”"

rows.original: She pauses. “Hard to believe I could run out of anything, with a whole ship to work with, but I had to fiddle with things to get the plumbing and life support going too. We still have to live down here and all that. But it all worked out better than I thought. I didn’t even know if I’d be able to rewire the bridge displays to make the hardlight cues for the pool tables.” She gives you a proud smile. “I made sure nothing got wasted. The old ship deserved that.”
rows.translation: 她顿了顿。“整艘飞船都能供我拆用，很难相信竟然还有东西会不够，不过为了让管道和生命维持系统运转，我也得摆弄各种设备。毕竟我们还得住在下面。但结果比预想中更好。我起初甚至不知道能否重新布线舰桥显示器，为台球桌制作硬光提示。”她朝你自豪一笑。“我确保没有任何东西遭到浪费。那艘旧船值得如此。”
rows.raw: "\n\nShe pauses. “Hard to believe I could run out of anything, with a whole ship to work with, but I had to fiddle with things to get the plumbing and life support going too. We still have to live down here and all that. But it all worked out better than I thought. I didn’t even know if I’d be able to rewire the bridge displays to make the hardlight cues for the pool tables.” She gives you a proud smile. “I made sure nothing got wasted. The old ship deserved that.”"

rows.original: What kind of ship did they have? It must have been big enough for a whole pirate crew, but you don’t recognize anything from the parts you’ve seen.
rows.translation: 她们以前拥有哪种飞船？它肯定足够容纳整队海盗，可你认不出见过的零件来自什么型号。
rows.raw: "\n\nWhat kind of ship did they have? It must have been big enough for a whole pirate crew, but you don’t recognize anything from the parts you’ve seen."

rows.original: A slow, wistful smile spreads across Kiki’s face. “We called her Melfina,” she says. “She was a Colt ZLX, a larger model from when Pyrite tried to do a more expensive version of the Colt line. Never really popular, but she had enough room for all of us, and damn, could those engines purr.”
rows.translation: 琪琪脸上缓缓浮现怀念的笑容。“我们叫她梅尔菲娜，”她说道。“她是一艘柯尔特ZLX，是黄铁工业尝试推出昂贵版柯尔特系列时生产的较大型号。从未真正流行起来，但有足够空间容纳所有人，而且那些引擎的轰鸣真他妈悦耳。”
rows.raw: "\n\nA slow, wistful smile spreads across Kiki’s face. “We called her Melfina,” she says. “She was a Colt ZLX, a larger model from when Pyrite tried to do a more expensive version of the Colt line. Never really popular, but she had enough room for all of us, and damn, could those engines purr.”"

rows.original: You can see how a Pyrite ship would be a good choice for a group of pirates. Plenty of cargo space, strong armor, and reliable engines are a good combination. Was that the only ship the crew ever had?
rows.translation: 你能理解为什么黄铁工业的飞船适合海盗团体。宽敞货舱、坚固装甲和可靠引擎的组合十分理想。那是这支船员唯一拥有过的飞船吗？
rows.raw: "\n\nYou can see how a Pyrite ship would be a good choice for a group of pirates. Plenty of cargo space, strong armor, and reliable engines are a good combination. Was that the only ship the crew ever had?"

rows.original: Kiki shrugs. “Not sure. She was the only ship they ever had when I was with them. But everything I learned about ship maintenance and repair was on her. The other techie, she was a veteran of some interplanetary war or another, but she knew that ship forwards and backwards.” She licks her upper lip. “That included every single place that vibrated, and how hard.”
rows.translation: 琪琪耸耸肩。“不确定。我加入她们期间，她是唯一一艘船。不过我所有飞船维护与维修知识都是在她身上学会的。另一名技术员参加过某场星际战争，是个老兵；她对那艘船的里里外外都了如指掌。”她舔了舔上唇。“包括每一个会震动的位置，以及震得有多猛烈。”
rows.raw: "\n\nKiki shrugs. “Not sure. She was the only ship they ever had when I was with them. But everything I learned about ship maintenance and repair was on her. The other techie, she was a veteran of some interplanetary war or another, but she knew that ship forwards and backwards.” She licks her upper lip. “That included every single place that vibrated, and how hard.”"

rows.original: You’re not surprised, but at the same time, they had a full crew, didn’t they? Why would they need to know where the ship vibrated?
rows.translation: 你并不意外，但与此同时，她们不是有完整船员吗？为什么还需要了解飞船哪里会震动？
rows.raw: "\n\nYou’re not surprised, but at the same time, they had a full crew, didn’t they? Why would they need to know where the ship vibrated?"

rows.original: “Sometimes you just want to get off without worrying about anyone else,” Kiki says. “And sometimes, when you’ve been up to your shoulders in the ship’s guts, sweaty and dirty and frustrated as hell, and you finally get things working again?” She gives you a look that would make an orgasming ultraporn star proud. “It’s a fucking rush. And after giving me that much trouble, I felt like Melfina damn well owed me at least one good hour of vibrating my balls.” She shrugs. “It was fine. I cleaned up when I was done.”
rows.translation: “有时你只是想自己释放，不必操心其他任何人，”琪琪说道。“而且有时，当你把双手深深埋进飞船内部，浑身汗水和污垢，沮丧得要命，最后终于让一切重新运转时？”她露出足以让正在高潮的超级色情明星都自愧不如的神情。“那他妈太刺激了。既然梅尔菲娜给我添了那么多麻烦，我觉得她至少欠我好好震动睾丸一个小时。”她耸耸肩。“没什么问题。我结束后清理干净了。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Sometimes you just want to get off without worrying about anyone else,” Kiki says. “And sometimes, when you’ve been up to your shoulders in the ship’s guts, sweaty and dirty and frustrated as hell, and you finally get things working again?” She gives you a look that would make an orgasming ultraporn star proud. “It’s a fucking rush. And after giving me that much trouble, I felt like Melfina damn well owed me at least one good hour of vibrating my balls.” She shrugs. “It was fine. I cleaned up when I was done.”"

rows.original: You can’t argue with that, and you’re not sure you want to. But it seems like they did the ship proud, by turning her into something new like this.
rows.translation: 你无法反驳，也不确定自己想不想反驳。不过把她改造成这样的全新事物，似乎确实没有辜负那艘船。
rows.raw: "\n\nYou can’t argue with that, and you’re not sure you want to. But it seems like they did the ship proud, by turning her into something new like this."

rows.original: “I think we did,” she says, and rests a hand on one of the metal panels bolted to the wall, admiration clear on her face. “She was never going to fly again, not after that last run. We barely got to this planet. I almost cried when I realized we had to take her apart, but there was nothing else we could do. It’s not like we had the money to leave a dead ship sitting in the spaceport.”
rows.translation: “我也觉得没有，”她说道，把手放在一块铆接到墙上的金属板上，脸上满是欣赏。“经历最后一次航程后，她绝不可能再次飞行。我们几乎无法抵达这颗星球。意识到必须拆解她时，我差点哭出来，可我们别无选择。我们根本没钱让一艘报废飞船一直占着太空港。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“I think we did,” she says, and rests a hand on one of the metal panels bolted to the wall, admiration clear on her face. “She was never going to fly again, not after that last run. We barely got to this planet. I almost cried when I realized we had to take her apart, but there was nothing else we could do. It’s not like we had the money to leave a dead ship sitting in the spaceport.”"

rows.original: Did they think about naming the bar after the ship? It seems like that would have been a good tribute.
rows.translation: 她们有没有考虑用飞船的名字为酒吧命名？那似乎会是很好的纪念。
rows.raw: "\n\nDid they think about naming the bar after the ship? It seems like that would have been a good tribute."

rows.original: “Nah,” Kiki says, shaking her head. “I wanted to leave her behind... I think I had to. Melfina was the ship, the whole ship, not just a bunch of parts. Even if we made good stuff with what was left.” She gives you a small smile. “I think this is about the best thing we could have done with her.”
rows.translation: “没有，”琪琪摇头说道。“我想把她留在过去...我觉得自己必须这样做。梅尔菲娜是那艘船，是完整的飞船，而不只是一堆零件。即使我们用剩余部分造出了不错的东西。”她淡淡地朝你微笑。“我觉得这大概是我们能为她安排的最好归宿。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Nah,” Kiki says, shaking her head. “I wanted to leave her behind... I think I had to. Melfina was the ship, the whole ship, not just a bunch of parts. Even if we made good stuff with what was left.” She gives you a small smile. “I think this is about the best thing we could have done with her.”"

rows.original: You ask Kiki what she thinks about Dhaal, now that she and the rest of the crew have been here for a few months. Being grounded must be pretty different from living in a ship.
rows.translation: 你问琪琪，她和其余船员在这里生活几个月后，对达尔有什么看法。困在地面上肯定与住在飞船里截然不同。
rows.raw: "You ask Kiki what she thinks about Dhaal, now that she and the rest of the crew have been here for a few months. Being grounded must be pretty different from living in a ship."

rows.original: “I don’t know if i’d call us grounded, even if we lost the ship,” Kiki says. She tilts her head and looks toward the ceiling. “It’s more like this is what we had to do, because things got a little too hot for us out there.” She shrugs. “And like I said, we could have done a lot worse. At least Dhaal isn’t some swamp planet or whatever.”
rows.translation: “就算我们失去了飞船，我也不会说自己被困在地面，”琪琪说道。她歪着头看向天花板。“更像是外面的情况对我们变得太过危险，所以这是我们必须做的事。”她耸耸肩。“而且就像我说的，我们可能落到更糟的地方。至少达尔不是什么沼泽星球之类的。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“I don’t know if i’d call us grounded, even if we lost the ship,” Kiki says. She tilts her head and looks toward the ceiling. “It’s more like this is what we had to do, because things got a little too hot for us out there.” She shrugs. “And like I said, we could have done a lot worse. At least Dhaal isn’t some swamp planet or whatever.”"

rows.original: So why did they pick Dhaal, anyway? The Rush has been on for long enough that they would have known enough about the planets to figure out which one to go for. Except maybe for Zhèng Shi, which kind of blew up.
rows.translation: 那么她们究竟为什么选择达尔？开拓潮已经持续了很久，她们应该掌握足够的星球情报，能够决定去哪里。也许郑石除外，那里突然变得极其热门。
rows.raw: "\n\nSo why did they pick Dhaal, anyway? The Rush has been on for long enough that they would have known enough about the planets to figure out which one to go for. Except maybe for Zhèng Shi, which kind of blew up."

rows.original: Kiki shakes her head quickly. “Oh, we were not going to Zhèng Shi. The last thing we needed to be was small fish in a big pond, and that place is loaded with slavers and worse.” She shudders. “I voted for Dhaal because it had an actual city and some kind of a real society on it.” She gestures at the dancing crowd. “The zaika were doing pretty good on their own before everybody else showed up.”
rows.translation: 琪琪迅速摇头。“噢，我们绝对不会去郑石。我们最不需要的就是去大池塘里当小鱼，那里到处都是奴隶贩子和更糟糕的家伙。”她浑身一颤。“我投票选择达尔，因为这里有真正的城市，还有某种真正的社会。”她朝跳舞的人群示意。“其他所有人出现以前，扎伊卡靠自己就过得相当不错。”
rows.raw: "\n\nKiki shakes her head quickly. “Oh, we were not going to Zhèng Shi. The last thing we needed to be was small fish in a big pond, and that place is loaded with slavers and worse.” She shudders. “I voted for Dhaal because it had an actual city and some kind of a real society on it.” She gestures at the dancing crowd. “The zaika were doing pretty good on their own before everybody else showed up.”"

rows.original: Before Kiki can say anything more, someone on the dance floor shouts loud enough to hear over the music. You and the dark woman both glance over, and see what looks like a fight about to start, with two of the zaika yelling and snarling at each other. Both of them are shaky, but it’s definitely about to get violent.
rows.translation: 琪琪还没来得及继续，舞池里就有人大喊，声音甚至盖过了音乐。你和那个深色皮肤的女人同时看去，只见两名扎伊卡彼此叫骂咆哮，眼看就要打起来。她们都站不太稳，但冲突显然马上就会变得暴力。
rows.raw: "\n\nBefore Kiki can say anything more, someone on the dance floor shouts loud enough to hear over the music. You and the dark woman both glance over, and see what looks like a fight about to start, with two of the zaika yelling and snarling at each other. Both of them are shaky, but it’s definitely about to get violent."

rows.original: “One sec,” Kiki says, and taps the side of her glasses. “Karrah? Kiki. Code two.” The music stops all at once. Kiki starts walking toward the dance floor, and holds her metal-bound hand out to one side. Two small stun batons slide out of the metal, sticking up between her fingers. Right as she reaches the zaika, Karrah comes rumbling into the room.
rows.translation: “等一下，”琪琪说道，轻敲眼镜侧面。“卡拉？我是琪琪，二号情况。”音乐立刻停止。琪琪开始走向舞池，把戴着金属装置的手伸向一侧。两根小型电击棍从金属中滑出，竖在手指之间。就在她抵达扎伊卡身边时，卡拉轰隆隆地走进房间。
rows.raw: "\n\n“One sec,” Kiki says, and taps the side of her glasses. “Karrah? Kiki. Code two.” The music stops all at once. Kiki starts walking toward the dance floor, and holds her metal-bound hand out to one side. Two small stun batons slide out of the metal, sticking up between her fingers. Right as she reaches the zaika, Karrah comes rumbling into the room."

rows.original: The muscular thraggen stands behind Kiki as she tells the zaika that they need to back off or get thrown out. Karrah growls at them, and flexes one arm. The metal ring around her bicep twitches, and more bands of metal slide down and out of it with a clattering sound, sheathing her entire arm in steel.
rows.translation: 肌肉发达的特拉根站在琪琪身后。琪琪告诉扎伊卡必须退开，否则就会被扔出去。卡拉朝她们咆哮，并弯曲一条手臂展示肌肉。她上臂的金属环抽动起来，更多金属带伴随哗啦声向下滑出，用钢铁包裹整条手臂。
rows.raw: "\n\nThe muscular thraggen stands behind Kiki as she tells the zaika that they need to back off or get thrown out. Karrah growls at them, and flexes one arm. The metal ring around her bicep twitches, and more bands of metal slide down and out of it with a clattering sound, sheathing her entire arm in steel."

rows.original: The two zaika women glare at each other for a moment, then spit a few insults, and it looks like they’re going to fight anyway. Then, they back away from each other, disappearing into the crowd. Kiki stands back as Karrah storms out, then looks at you with a smile.
rows.translation: 两名扎伊卡女人彼此怒视片刻，随后吐出几句侮辱，看起来仍打算动手。但接着，她们各自后退，消失在人群中。卡拉气冲冲地离开，琪琪则退到一旁，随后微笑着看向你。
rows.raw: "The two zaika women glare at each other for a moment, then spit a few insults, and it looks like they’re going to fight anyway. Then, they back away from each other, disappearing into the crowd. Kiki stands back as Karrah storms out, then looks at you with a smile."

rows.original: One of the zaika women screeches and leaps for the other, and Karrah snarls as she yanks them apart. Kiki steps back, stun batons at the ready, but Karrah wrestles the zaika to the ground, then puts the struggling woman over her shoulder and hauls her out. Kiki returns to you, frowning.
rows.translation: 其中一名扎伊卡女人尖叫着扑向另一个，卡拉咆哮一声，将她们强行分开。琪琪退后一步，电击棍蓄势待发，但卡拉把扎伊卡摔倒在地，随后将仍在挣扎的女人扛到肩上拖了出去。琪琪皱着眉头回到你身边。
rows.raw: "One of the zaika women screeches and leaps for the other, and Karrah snarls as she yanks them apart. Kiki steps back, stun batons at the ready, but Karrah wrestles the zaika to the ground, then puts the struggling woman over her shoulder and hauls her out. Kiki returns to you, frowning."

rows.original: The two zaika women glare at each other for a moment, then leap at each other and start kissing. One loops her leg around the other’s waist as they make out on the dance floor, their tails twisting around each other. Kiki and Karrah both step back, and give each other amused looks. When she turns back to you, she’s grinning.
rows.translation: 两名扎伊卡女人彼此怒视片刻，随后扑向对方，开始接吻。其中一人在热吻时用腿环住另一人的腰，尾巴也彼此缠绕。琪琪和卡拉同时后退，互相投去觉得好笑的目光。等她转回来看你时，脸上正挂着笑容。
rows.raw: "The two zaika women glare at each other for a moment, then leap at each other and start kissing. One loops her leg around the other’s waist as they make out on the dance floor, their tails twisting around each other. Kiki and Karrah both step back, and give each other amused looks. When she turns back to you, she’s grinning."

rows.original: “Never know how that’s going to turn out,” Kiki says, then taps her glasses to start the music again.
rows.translation: “永远不知道这种事最后会怎么发展，”琪琪说道，随后轻敲眼镜，重新开始播放音乐。
rows.raw: "\n\n“Never know how that’s going to turn out,” Kiki says, then taps her glasses to start the music again."

rows.original: She returns to her usual place to watch the dance floor, and doesn’t seem to want to say much more.
rows.translation: 她回到平时监视舞池的位置，似乎不想再多说什么。
rows.raw: " She returns to her usual place to watch the dance floor, and doesn’t seem to want to say much more."

rows.original: Kiki probably has more to say about this, but not right now. Maybe if you spend more time at the bar, she’ll feel more like opening up to you.
rows.translation: 琪琪大概还有更多话可说，但不是现在。或许你在酒吧多待些日子以后，她会更愿意向你敞开心扉。
rows.raw: "\n\nKiki probably has more to say about this, but not right now. Maybe if you spend more time at the bar, she’ll feel more like opening up to you."

rows.original: “First week we were here, we had four different fights break out, and every night, I wondered what we’d gotten ourselves into.”
rows.translation: “我们抵达这里的第一周就爆发了四场不同的斗殴。每个晚上，我都会怀疑我们究竟让自己陷入了什么处境。”
rows.raw: " “First week we were here, we had four different fights break out, and every night, I wondered what we’d gotten ourselves into.”"

rows.original: She returns to her usual place to watch the dance floor, then taps the side of her glasses again. A holographic projection of the dance room appears in the air in front of her, rows of text sliding down the sides. Kiki peers at it for a moment, then makes it disappear and looks at you.
rows.translation: 她回到平时监视舞池的位置，随后再次轻敲眼镜侧面。一幅舞厅的全息投影出现在面前的空中，两侧不断滑下成排文字。琪琪观察片刻，让投影消失，随后看向你。
rows.raw: "\n\nShe returns to her usual place to watch the dance floor, then taps the side of her glasses again. A holographic projection of the dance room appears in the air in front of her, rows of text sliding down the sides. Kiki peers at it for a moment, then makes it disappear and looks at you."

rows.original: “Had to make sure we got that on camera,” she says. “If someone’s a real problem all the time, we make sure they don’t get in here again.”
rows.translation: “必须确保摄像头拍到了刚才的事，”她说道。“如果某个人总是造成严重麻烦，我们会确保他们再也进不来。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Had to make sure we got that on camera,” she says. “If someone’s a real problem all the time, we make sure they don’t get in here again.”"

rows.original: Has that been a problem? Running an underground bar like this, they’re sure to get some people who show up just looking for a fight.
rows.translation: 这一直是个问题吗？经营这样的地下酒吧，她们肯定会遇到一些专门来打架的人。
rows.raw: "\n\nHas that been a problem? Running an underground bar like this, they’re sure to get some people who show up just looking for a fight."

rows.original: “If this was anywhere else, yeah, that’d be a real big thing,” Kiki says. “But the way the zaika are, most of them don’t get violent when they’re on milk.” She leans in closer to you and lowers her voice. “When they’re off milk, that’s a different story. For some of them, anyway. But it hasn’t been bad since we got rid of the real troublemakers. Look, I even made a chart for it.”
rows.translation: “如果这是其他地方，没错，那会是个大问题，”琪琪说道。“不过扎伊卡就是这样，喝奶以后，大多数人不会变得暴力。”她靠近你，压低声音。“断奶时就是另一回事了。至少有些人会这样。不过自从我们赶走真正的麻烦人物后，情况已经不坏了。看，我甚至为此做了张图表。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“If this was anywhere else, yeah, that’d be a real big thing,” Kiki says. “But the way the zaika are, most of them don’t get violent when they’re on milk.” She leans in closer to you and lowers her voice. “When they’re off milk, that’s a different story. For some of them, anyway. But it hasn’t been bad since we got rid of the real troublemakers. Look, I even made a chart for it.”"

rows.original: Kiki taps her glasses once more, and her holograms bring up a chart that looks like a stock that’s in the process of tanking. It’s clearly not that, though, if the smile on her face is any sign. “I started keeping track of how many fights we had after that first week, when we started throwing out problem people and keeping them out. We just had a few real assholes ruining the party for everyone,” she continues, pointing to the chart as it trends down, “and once we got rid of them, people fought a lot less.”
rows.translation: 琪琪再次轻敲眼镜，全息影像显示出一张看起来像正在暴跌的股票走势图。不过从她脸上的笑容判断，那显然不是股票。“第一周之后，我们开始扔出惹事的人并禁止他们入内，我也从那时开始记录斗殴次数。之前只是几个真正的混蛋破坏了所有人的派对，”她一边继续说道，一边指向不断下降的曲线，“等我们赶走那些人，斗殴就少多了。”
rows.raw: "\n\nKiki taps her glasses once more, and her holograms bring up a chart that looks like a stock that’s in the process of tanking. It’s clearly not that, though, if the smile on her face is any sign. “I started keeping track of how many fights we had after that first week, when we started throwing out problem people and keeping them out. We just had a few real assholes ruining the party for everyone,” she continues, pointing to the chart as it trends down, “and once we got rid of them, people fought a lot less.”"

rows.original: Not bad. But keeping track of this doesn’t seem like the kind of thing you’d expect from a pirate in an underground bar.
rows.translation: 做得不错。不过记录这些，似乎不像地下酒吧里的海盗会做的事。
rows.raw: "\n\nNot bad. But keeping track of this doesn’t seem like the kind of thing you’d expect from a pirate in an underground bar."

rows.original: She looks at you, wide-eyed. “You mean you didn’t notice I’m kind of a geek about this stuff?” She giggles at you. “Okay, I started this as a test of some cheap tracking and charting software I swiped along with a bunch of bank accounts and porn, but it’s useful, I swear.”
rows.translation: 她睁大眼睛看着你。“你是说，你没注意到我在这类事情上有点技术宅吗？”她冲你咯咯笑道。“好吧，我起初只是想测试一款廉价的追踪制表软件，是和一堆银行账户及色情片一起顺来的，但我发誓它真的很有用。”
rows.raw: "\n\nShe looks at you, wide-eyed. “You mean you didn’t notice I’m kind of a geek about this stuff?” She giggles at you. “Okay, I started this as a test of some cheap tracking and charting software I swiped along with a bunch of bank accounts and porn, but it’s useful, I swear.”"

rows.original: Kiki glances toward the bar room. “Monika wants us running this place like an actual business, not some trashy spacer dive that disappears after a month or two. If we’re going to be here for a while, we need to keep track of things like this.”
rows.translation: 琪琪朝酒吧大厅看去。“莫妮卡希望我们把这里当作真正的生意来经营，而不是那种一两个月就会消失的破烂太空客酒吧。如果要在这里待上一阵子，我们就得记录这类事情。”
rows.raw: "\n\nKiki glances toward the bar room. “Monika wants us running this place like an actual business, not some trashy spacer dive that disappears after a month or two. If we’re going to be here for a while, we need to keep track of things like this.”"

rows.original: [flags.MASTODON_END|Does she know how much longer they plan to be here?|Do they plan to be here for a long time?]
rows.translation: [flags.MASTODON_END|她知不知道她们还打算在这里待多久？|她们打算在这里待很长时间吗？]
rows.raw: "\n\n[flags.MASTODON_END|Does she know how much longer they plan to be here?|Do they plan to be here for a long time?]"

rows.original: She looks like she’s about to say something, then pauses and shrugs. “Who knows?” Kiki says, then looks back to the dancing crowd.
rows.translation: 她看起来正想说些什么，却又停下来耸耸肩。“谁知道呢？”琪琪说道，随后重新看向跳舞的人群。
rows.raw: "\n\nShe looks like she’s about to say something, then pauses and shrugs. “Who knows?” Kiki says, then looks back to the dancing crowd."

rows.original: It seems like she has more to say on that, but doesn’t want to right now. Maybe if you spend more time at the bar, she’ll feel more like opening up to you.
rows.translation: 看来她对此还有更多话想说，只是现在不愿开口。或许你在酒吧多待些日子以后，她会更愿意向你敞开心扉。
rows.raw: "\n\nIt seems like she has more to say on that, but doesn’t want to right now. Maybe if you spend more time at the bar, she’ll feel more like opening up to you."

rows.original: Do they plan to be here for a long time?
rows.translation: 她们打算长期留在这里吗？
rows.raw: "\n\nDo they plan to be here for a long time?"

rows.original: “It[flags.MASTODON_END|’s hard to say| seems like that sometimes,]” Kiki says, and her voice goes lower again. “Monika’s[flags.MASTODON_END| been] real happy here. She doesn’t say much about how she feels, but she[flags.MASTODON_END| was|’s] actually relaxed. She was never relaxed as a captain.” She frowns. “It’s a little weird[flags.MASTODON_END| seeing her stressed about stuff again].”
rows.translation: “这[flags.MASTODON_END|很难说|有时看起来确实如此，]”琪琪说道，声音再次压低。“莫妮卡在这里[flags.MASTODON_END|一直]非常开心。她不怎么谈自己的感受，但她[flags.MASTODON_END|以前|现在]真的很放松。她当船长时从来没有放松过。”她皱起眉头。“[flags.MASTODON_END|看见她又开始为事情操心，]感觉有点奇怪。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“It[flags.MASTODON_END|’s hard to say| seems like that sometimes,]” Kiki says, and her voice goes lower again. “Monika’s[flags.MASTODON_END| been] real happy here. She doesn’t say much about how she feels, but she[flags.MASTODON_END| was|’s] actually relaxed. She was never relaxed as a captain.” She frowns. “It’s a little weird[flags.MASTODON_END| seeing her stressed about stuff again].”"

rows.original: What about the rest of the crew? And what about her?
rows.translation: 其他船员呢？还有她自己呢？
rows.raw: "\n\nWhat about the rest of the crew? And what about her?"

rows.original: Kiki takes a deep breath, enough to make her vest’s buttons strain against her generous chest. “Josie’s happy pretty much anywhere[flags.MASTODON_END|, so she’s ready whenever]. Must be nice, really. But she’s[flags.MASTODON_END| still] getting her titties worked all day, and all the attention and dick she wants, so she’s good.” Kiki smiles a little, and adjusts the bulge at the front of her pants.
rows.translation: 琪琪深吸一口气，宽厚的胸部撑得背心纽扣绷紧。“乔茜基本在哪里都能开心[flags.MASTODON_END|，所以随时都准备好了]。说真的，真让人羡慕。不过她[flags.MASTODON_END|依然]整天都有人照料乳房，也能得到想要的一切关注和鸡巴，所以她过得不错。”琪琪微微一笑，调整了一下裤子前面的鼓包。
rows.raw: "\n\nKiki takes a deep breath, enough to make her vest’s buttons strain against her generous chest. “Josie’s happy pretty much anywhere[flags.MASTODON_END|, so she’s ready whenever]. Must be nice, really. But she’s[flags.MASTODON_END| still] getting her titties worked all day, and all the attention and dick she wants, so she’s good.” Kiki smiles a little, and adjusts the bulge at the front of her pants."

rows.original: “Karrah[flags.MASTODON_END| still] gets to snarl and threaten people and beat them up if they don’t play nice, and whenever we head into the city, she gets to play bodyguard and beat up those weirdos who keep trying to milk us. So she’s having a good time, but I [flags.MASTODON_END|know she’s looking forward to getting out there and beating people up again|think she misses actual fights, and most of the gangs don’t want to mess with her so it’s not like she’s got anyone who can give her a challenge]. It’s kind of a long way from breaking down ship doors to guarding a club’s door.”
rows.translation: “卡拉[flags.MASTODON_END|依然]可以咆哮、威胁别人，要是有人不守规矩还能揍他们；每次我们进城，她都能充当保镖，把那些总想给我们挤奶的怪人打一顿。所以她过得很开心，不过我[flags.MASTODON_END|知道她很期待重新出去揍人|觉得她怀念真正的战斗，而且大多数帮派都不愿招惹她，所以也没人能给她一点挑战]。这和撞开飞船舱门相比，守着一家俱乐部的门差得可远了。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Karrah[flags.MASTODON_END| still] gets to snarl and threaten people and beat them up if they don’t play nice, and whenever we head into the city, she gets to play bodyguard and beat up those weirdos who keep trying to milk us. So she’s having a good time, but I [flags.MASTODON_END|know she’s looking forward to getting out there and beating people up again|think she misses actual fights, and most of the gangs don’t want to mess with her so it’s not like she’s got anyone who can give her a challenge]. It’s kind of a long way from breaking down ship doors to guarding a club’s door.”"

rows.original: Kiki sighs, and looks at you. “And me? I’m [flags.MASTODON_END|looking forward to getting out of here|doing okay]. Dhaal’s[flags.MASTODON_END| been] interesting, [flags.MASTODON_END|even if it’s not the best place to get stuck|and I could probably get a legit job here if I wanted to, or find work on a ship that’s heading out.]” She gestures at the room, and smiles. “But one of the best things about being a pirate is that you’re free, and we’ve still got that. We’re out of reach of the corps and the gangs and everybody else, and we’re doing what we want to do. All in a place that we built out of our old ship. Okay, I’m the one who figured out most of it, but we still built it together. And....”
rows.translation: 琪琪叹了口气，看向你。“至于我？我[flags.MASTODON_END|很期待离开这里|过得还行]。达尔[flags.MASTODON_END|一直]挺有意思，[flags.MASTODON_END|就算这里不是最适合受困的地方|而且如果我愿意，大概能在这里找份正经工作，或者去即将启航的飞船上干活。]”她朝房间示意，露出笑容。“不过当海盗最好的一点，就是你很自由，而我们仍然拥有自由。企业、帮派和其他所有人都管不到我们，我们想做什么就做什么。更何况这里还是用我们的旧飞船建成的。好吧，大部分办法都是我想出来的，但我们依然一起建成了这里。而且....”
rows.raw: "\n\nKiki sighs, and looks at you. “And me? I’m [flags.MASTODON_END|looking forward to getting out of here|doing okay]. Dhaal’s[flags.MASTODON_END| been] interesting, [flags.MASTODON_END|even if it’s not the best place to get stuck|and I could probably get a legit job here if I wanted to, or find work on a ship that’s heading out.]” She gestures at the room, and smiles. “But one of the best things about being a pirate is that you’re free, and we’ve still got that. We’re out of reach of the corps and the gangs and everybody else, and we’re doing what we want to do. All in a place that we built out of our old ship. Okay, I’m the one who figured out most of it, but we still built it together. And....”"

rows.original: She pauses for a moment, and frowns a little, looking wistful. “I[flags.MASTODON_END|’ll be a little sad to leave this place| don’t know if I could leave these girls] behind. It’s only been a few [flags.MASTODON_END|months|years], but I feel like [flags.MASTODON_END|we did something good down here|I’ve been with them forever]. [flags.MASTODON_END|There’s all kinds of ways this could have gone, but we pulled it together and made something this place really needed|They’re the only ones who didn’t want to break up the crew, and I don’t want to be the one who ruins what we’ve got together].”
rows.translation: 她停顿片刻，略微皱眉，神情惆怅。“我[flags.MASTODON_END|离开这里时会有点难过|不知道自己能不能把这些姑娘]抛在身后。虽然才过了几[flags.MASTODON_END|个月|年]，但我觉得[flags.MASTODON_END|我们在这里做了件好事|自己已经和她们在一起很久了]。[flags.MASTODON_END|这件事本来可能出现各种结果，但我们齐心协力，创造出了这里真正需要的东西|只有她们不想拆散船员，我也不想成为破坏我们共同拥有的一切的人]。”
rows.raw: "\n\nShe pauses for a moment, and frowns a little, looking wistful. “I[flags.MASTODON_END|’ll be a little sad to leave this place| don’t know if I could leave these girls] behind. It’s only been a few [flags.MASTODON_END|months|years], but I feel like [flags.MASTODON_END|we did something good down here|I’ve been with them forever]. rows.original: You ask Kiki how things are going with the new ship, and her eyes light up when the words are barely out of your mouth. “Okay, how much time do you have?” Kiki asks, talking faster than usual. “Because I can go on about this all day. And I will. Ask any of the other girls.” You do have other things to do, so you can’t spend a day listening to her, but you can take a little time. Maybe she can sum it up? She grins at you, then taps the edge of her glasses, queueing up another dozen songs or so for the dance. Then, she rubs her hands together and starts talking. “It’s amazing. It really is. Don’t get me wrong, having the old ship was great, and I learned a lot from working on Melfina. Even when we had to take her apart.” A frown touches her lips, but disappears quickly. “But this is different. The Starhammer’s a larger model, and there’s a lot we can do with a ship that size and only four of us on it.” The ship did seem pretty roomy when it was just you and a bunch of robots trying to kill you, so you can see how it would have plenty of room for the crew. “Oh yeah,” Kiki says. “Plenty of space for, like, everything I want to do. And more than that, it’s ours. Just the four of us, probably more because Monika says she wants more crew, but right now we can do whatever we want with it.” Her eyes narrow as she grins at you. “And I have plans.” What kind of plans? If that devious look on her face means anything.... Kiki laughs out loud. “You have no idea. I’ve been doing all kinds of research for stuff we can add. The rec room’s got a halfway decent setup but I can make it into so much more.” Like what? She holds up her right hand, and starts counting off on her metal-bound fingers. “First, Monika’s been all kinds of stressed about this. She acts like it’s no big deal, but I can tell. So I found these full-body capsule things that do a personal steam bath.” Kiki pauses, barely catching a breath. “I had to go with the larger ones so they could fit Karrah, but they’re going to be awesome.” That sounds like a good start. What else? “Since Josie’s not going to be getting her tits sucked on all day, which is really too bad, I got a kickass deal on a milker for her,” Kiki says. “Seriously, this thing’s incredible. It’s got seven different suction settings, massagers and vibrators, and stores like five or six gallons before you have to empty it.” She pauses, and blinks like something just occurred to her. “I have no idea what her actual output is,” she mutters. “Huh. I’ll have to ask and see if I can mod that thing when it gets here.” Yeah, that sounds like something she should figure out. Wouldn’t do much good to have the thing overflow the first time Josie used it. Kiki winces. “No kidding,” she says. “I like the new ship smell, having the whole place smell like milk would get old real quick.” She brushes a lock of blue hair behind one pointed ear and continues. “Anyway, I also got a deal on a VR rig that’s a major upgrade for the rec room, and some fighting games for Karrah. I know we’ll get into actual fights again once we’re flying, but who knows when that’ll happen, and I know she misses punching people.” How strong is the VR setup? Karrah could probably break a regular one without even trying. The grin Kiki gives you has much more of an edge to it. Whatever she has in mind, she clearly loves it. “Trust me, I got the sturdiest machine I could find,” she says. “Because there’s this startup in New Texas working on the highest fucking quality VR sex rigs you can imagine.” You can imagine quite a bit, especially where New Texans are concerned. That must be some durable equipment. “They say it’s all locally made and tested. I’ve partied on New Texas before, so if it can handle them, it can handle this crew.” She leans in and gives you a nudge, looking ridiculously happy. “I swear, I’m going to ride the hell out of that thing so I can remember what it’s like to get my vag fucked and not have to worry about getting pregged. I mean, I know I could use a dildo, but it’s not the same if it doesn’t feel like there’s a body attached, you know?” You chuckle. If that’s not a goal for VR sex, at least for her, you don’t know what is. But it sounds like she’s got everything well in hand for fixing up the ship. “Yeah, I’ve got all the mundane stuff under control,” she says with a shrug. “But I didn’t want to bore you with thruster parts and console screens and all that basic junk. You already saw that when you brought it in.” That you did. But it’s good to know the ship’s in good hands, and you hope it’ll be up and running soon. Kiki winces. “I don’t know about soon, but it’ll happen,” she says. “Monika says we need to get the essentials done and functional before working on the fun stuff.” Some of the delight fades from her face, and she looks a little more serious. It’s clear she knows there’s still a lot left to do. Then, she gives you a genuine smile. “But thank you, again, for getting the ship for us. There’s no way we could have done this without you.”
rows.translation: 你问琪琪新飞船的情况如何，话才刚出口，她的双眼就亮了起来。 “好吧，你有多少时间？”琪琪问道，语速比平时更快。“因为这件事我能说上一整天。而且我真的会说。你可以问问其他姑娘。” 你还有其他事要做，所以不能花上一天听她说，但抽出一点时间没问题。也许她能概括一下？ 她冲你咧嘴一笑，随后轻敲眼镜边缘，又给舞池排了十几首歌。接着，她搓了搓双手，开始滔滔不绝。 “太棒了。真的太棒了。别误会，拥有旧飞船的感觉也很好，我在梅尔菲娜号上工作时学到了很多东西。即使后来我们不得不拆掉她。”一丝愁容掠过她的唇角，却很快消失。“但这不一样。星锤号的型号更大，而这么大一艘船上只有我们四个，能做的事情可多了。” 当时船里只有你和一群想杀死你的机器人，那艘船确实显得相当宽敞，所以你能想象船员们会有充足的空间。 “没错，”琪琪说道。“我想做的所有事情，差不多都有足够空间。更重要的是，它属于我们。只有我们四个，也许以后会更多，因为莫妮卡说她想招募更多船员，不过现在我们想怎么改就怎么改。”她眯起眼睛，冲你咧嘴笑道。“而且我有不少计划。” 什么样的计划？如果她脸上那副狡黠神情意味着什么.... 琪琪放声大笑。“你根本想象不到。我一直在研究各种能加装的东西。娱乐室目前的配置还算过得去，但我能把它改得好得多。” 比如呢？ 她举起右手，开始用戴着金属装置的手指数起来。“首先，莫妮卡一直为这件事操心得要命。她装得好像没什么大不了，但我看得出来。所以我找到了这种可以提供私人蒸汽浴的全身舱。”琪琪停了一下，勉强喘了口气。“为了装得下卡拉，我必须选择更大的型号，不过它们肯定会非常棒。” 听起来是个不错的开始。还有呢？ “乔茜以后没法整天让人吸奶了，真是太遗憾了，所以我给她淘到了一台特别划算的挤奶器，”琪琪说道。“说真的，这东西太厉害了。它有七档不同的吸力设置、按摩器和振动器，而且倒空之前能储存五六加仑。”她顿了一下，眨眨眼睛，仿佛突然想到了什么。“我根本不知道她实际能产多少奶，”她低声说道。“嗯。等东西送到后，我得问问她，再看看能不能改装。” 没错，这确实是她该弄清楚的事。要是乔茜第一次使用就让那东西溢出来，可没什么用。 琪琪缩了缩脸。“可不是嘛，”她说道。“我喜欢新飞船的气味，但整艘船闻起来都像奶，很快就会腻了。”她把一绺蓝发拨到尖耳后，继续说道。“总之，我还淘到了一套VR设备，对娱乐室来说是一次重大升级，另外还有几款给卡拉玩的格斗游戏。我知道等我们再次起飞后肯定还会遇上真正的战斗，可谁知道那要等到什么时候，而且我知道她很想念揍人的感觉。” 那套VR设备有多结实？卡拉大概不费吹灰之力就能弄坏普通设备。 琪琪冲你露出的笑容多了几分邪气。不管她想到了什么，她显然非常喜欢。“相信我，我找的是能买到的最结实的机器，”她说道。“因为新德州有家初创公司正在研发你能想象到的最高品质的性爱VR设备。” 你能想象的东西相当多，尤其当事情涉及新德州人时。那一定是相当耐用的设备。 “他们说所有东西都在当地制造并经过测试。我以前在新德州狂欢过，所以只要它扛得住他们，就扛得住这群船员。”她凑近撞了你一下，看起来开心得不得了。“我发誓，我会狠狠骑那东西，好让自己重新体会阴道被干、又不必担心怀孕是什么滋味。我是说，我知道自己可以用假阳具，但如果感觉不到它连着一具身体，就完全不是一回事，你懂吧？” 你轻笑起来。如果这都不算性爱VR的目标，至少对她而言，你就不知道什么才算了。不过听起来，她已经把整修飞船的一切安排妥当。 “没错，那些普通事务我都处理好了，”她耸耸肩说道。“不过我不想拿推进器零件、控制台屏幕和那些基础杂物来烦你。你把船送来时已经见过了。” 你的确见过。不过知道飞船得到了妥善照料还是很好，你希望它能尽快恢复运行。 琪琪缩了缩脸。“我不知道能不能算尽快，但总会完成的，”她说道。“莫妮卡说，我们必须先把必要的东西修好并恢复功能，再去处理好玩的部分。”她脸上的喜悦消退了几分，神情也变得略微严肃。显然，她知道还有很多工作要做。 接着，她真诚地朝你微笑。“不过还是要再次谢谢你帮我们弄到飞船。没有你，我们绝对办不到。”

rows.original: You tell Monika that you got an e-mail from Kiki, and it sounded important. Is the crew in some kind of trouble? There’s a slow change in Monika’s demeanor once you ask. The friendly bartender’s smile fades, replaced by a stern expression you’ve never seen before. Her organic eye flicks back and forth, and she nods to you, then reaches up and puts one hand to her ear. “All crew,” she says. “Code white.” A moment later, the music from the dance room fades and goes quiet, and the multicolored lights shift to a medium white. The blue and yellow lights in the bar do the same, casting the place in a harsher color. The former ship’s hull shines on the wall, gray and black and red, the stark steel no longer hidden behind the bar’s flashy lights and mood. Zaika voices rise in a wave of grumbling and whining. It’s clear they know what this means — the bar is closing, time for everyone to go. Many of them down their mugs of milk, with a few stumbling away from their tables, held up by a friend or two. The hall leading out of the bar fills with a wave of dark-skinned figures as the sweaty dancers filter out of the other room, Kiki behind them, waving her arms as she encourages them to get going. Behind the bar, Josie slides a bunch of shot glasses into a sink beneath the counter and starts the water, giving you a clear view of her freckled ass and bare pussy as she bends over. It doesn’t seem like she’s trying to tempt you, this is just how she is. Once she’s done, she leans up against the bar and smiles at you, but she looks a little worried, the expression out of place on her. Kiki strolls over to the bar, and gives you a sly grin. The bulge in her pants twitches in your direction, but instead of making one of her usual lascivious comments, she throws one leg over a stool and looks to Monika as she sits. “Dance room’s clear,” Kiki says. “Is this about what I think it is?” When Monika nods at her, Kiki fiddles with the edge of her glasses. “Sweet. I’ll pull up the files.” She’s all business, and you can see some of the focus that makes her a skilled hacker. The sound of zaika chatter coming from the hallway fades after another minute or two, accompanied by Karrah’s stern, growly voice. There’s a loud clap that was probably her hand on some zaika girl’s ass, and a moment later, the hulking thraggen stalks into the room, her tusks sticking up as she grumbles. Karrah nods to you, then leans up against the wall next to the doorway, her arms folded beneath her enormous rack. Seeing the bar crew under the plain lights drives home the kind of life they have here. The Crash Landing might be a hell of a bar when it’s party time, but it’s still a few concrete rooms with metal bolted to the walls, buried beneath a city where people would hunt the crew just because they can make milk. It’s hard for them to go above ground without finding trouble. And now, they’ve got some reason to ask for your help. “Door sealed, Karrah?” Monika asks, looking across the room. Karrah nods with a grunt. “All closed up, as per usual,” she says. There’s a harshness to her voice that’s not usually there, even when she’s being the bouncer. “Good.” Monika twirls a shot glass between her fingers, then glances around at everyone and puts the glass away. She turns her serious look on you. “I’m glad you’re here, [pc.name]. Something’s come up, and you might be the only person we know who can help.” [pc.nmh |Whatever it is, you’ll be glad to help if you can. They’ve been good to you, and you’d like to return the favor. |You can’t promise anything, but you’ll listen, especially for the bar and the crew. Last I heard, she’d found herself a new crew and somehow got hold of a ship, and was trying to go legit.” “Shipping’s good work if you can get it,” Josie adds, then smooths down the front of her apron. “At least, that’s what I heard at the dock back home. We didn’t really see any freighters.” Monika’s ears twitch toward Josie, then she continues. “But it looks like Redd ran into some trouble with her last run. Her distress call said something about sabotage, and a problem with some robots she was carrying.” Kiki shakes her head. “That’s a real easy way to get into trouble, carrying robots with any kind of guns or whatever. Someone decides they want to fuck you over, all they’ve got to do is hack into the bots, and suddenly they’ve got an army.” “That’s fucking cowardly,” Karrah mutters. “Take over the ship your damn self.” A faint smile flickers across Monika’s lips, then disappears. “It’s not as easy as Kiki makes it sound, but it could be that’s what happened.” She frowns, then looks away, and some of the sternness fades from her expression. “It’s been a long time since I’ve heard from Redd, since any of us have. If she reached out to me, she must be in serious trouble.” Karrah snorts, loud enough to echo in the concrete room. “Shows how much good going legit did her. Doesn’t she have some trader friends with a big fucking gunship by now? Maybe a merc group?” Monika narrows her organic eye at Karrah. “Do you have a problem with this, Karrah?” “She fucked off and left us here,” Karrah snarls. “You think she’d come for us if we sent her a distress call?” “She would,” Josie says, sincerity plain on her face. She clenches her hands into her milk-spotted apron, and looks more worried than you’ve ever seen her. “She absolutely would,” Monika says, staring down Karrah. “We all know what happened, no point in going over it again. But Redd’s still crew. 琪琪摆弄眼镜，一道全息投影从圆形镜片发出光芒。棱角分明的货船出现在吧台上方的空气里，通体亮蓝，尽是硬朗线条与角度。飞船分为两个主要部分，后部大于前部，中间区域狭窄，前端则有三角形驾驶舱。 “瑞德的船员驾驶一艘黄铁工业的星锤号，没什么特别，不过货舱空间巨大。这艘船很适合运输，主要因为引擎设计意味着它在载重较大时不会损失太多动力或速度——” 莫妮卡清了清嗓子，琪琪略微脸红，继续讲述，没有再次沉迷于飞船的技术细节。乔茜咯咯笑着低声重复“载重”。 “总之，”琪琪说道，“我们有瑞德飞船的坐标和追踪信息，所以靠近后就能找到。她们管它叫乳齿象号。”她停下来，把视线移开一阵，随后继续。“我们不知道你抵达时会发现什么，因为第一次呼叫后，就再没收到她的消息。”她上下打量你，但感觉更像在评估能力，而非欣赏身体。“希望情况不会太糟，不过我非常确定你能应付一些机器人。” 你问，她们是否认为黑色虚空是幕后黑手，毕竟那群人在大家分开以前一直追捕她们。所有船员一同畏缩，过了一会儿才有人回答。 “希望不是，”莫妮卡说道。“我不能要求你和他们交手。如果你抵达后发现那里像是他们的手笔，我不会因为你立刻离开而责怪你。但希望这只是某个竞争货运商想除掉对手。” “或者某种严重技术故障，又或者一颗流浪小行星摧毁了她们的护盾，诸如此类，”琪琪迅速说道。她听起来十分紧张，似乎正努力寻找自己能够解决的问题，以此隐藏不安。 “我觉得我们没那么走运，”卡拉嘟囔道，没有再说什么。 “我只希望她们平安，”乔茜补充道。 “我们都希望如此，”莫妮卡说道。她若有所思地望向你，用天然眼睛牢牢注视。“所以你觉得怎么样，[pc.name]？我们没有飞船，而且不能就这样放弃这里跟你一起去，否则酒吧可能会落进某些城市拾荒者手中。会来这里的人当中，只有你或许能应付那艘船上的一切。你愿意帮我们这个忙吗？”
rows.raw: " You tell Monika that you got an e-mail from Kiki, and it sounded important. Is the crew in some kind of trouble? There’s a slow change in Monika’s demeanor once you ask. The friendly bartender’s smile fades, replaced by a stern expression you’ve never seen before. Her organic eye flicks back and forth, and she nods to you, then reaches up and puts one hand to her ear. “All crew,” she says. “Code white.” A moment later, the music from the dance room fades and goes quiet, and the multicolored lights shift to a medium white. The blue and yellow lights in the bar do the same, casting the place in a harsher color. The former ship’s hull shines on the wall, gray and black and red, the stark steel no longer hidden behind the bar’s flashy lights and mood. Zaika voices rise in a wave of grumbling and whining. It’s clear they know what this means — the bar is closing, time for everyone to go. Many of them down their mugs of milk, with a few stumbling away from their tables, held up by a friend or two. The hall leading out of the bar fills with a wave of dark-skinned figures as the sweaty dancers filter out of the other room, Kiki behind them, waving her arms as she encourages them to get going. Behind the bar, Josie slides a bunch of shot glasses into a sink beneath the counter and starts the water, giving you a clear view of her freckled ass and bare pussy as she bends over. It doesn’t seem like she’s trying to tempt you, this is just how she is. Once she’s done, she leans up against the bar and smiles at you, but she looks a little worried, the expression out of place on her. Kiki strolls over to the bar, and gives you a sly grin. The bulge in her pants twitches in your direction, but instead of making one of her usual lascivious comments, she throws one leg over a stool and looks to Monika as she sits. “Dance room’s clear,” Kiki says. “Is this about what I think it is?” When Monika nods at her, Kiki fiddles with the edge of her glasses. “Sweet. I’ll pull up the files.” She’s all business, and you can see some of the focus that makes her a skilled hacker. The sound of zaika chatter coming from the hallway fades after another minute or two, accompanied by Karrah’s stern, growly voice. There’s a loud clap that was probably her hand on some zaika girl’s ass, and a moment later, the hulking thraggen stalks into the room, her tusks sticking up as she grumbles. Karrah nods to you, then leans up against the wall next to the doorway, her arms folded beneath her enormous rack. Seeing the bar crew under the plain lights drives home the kind of life they have here. The Crash Landing might be a hell of a bar when it’s party time, but it’s still a few concrete rooms with metal bolted to the walls, buried beneath a city where people would hunt the crew just because they can make milk. It’s hard for them to go above ground without finding trouble. And now, they’ve got some reason to ask for your help. “Door sealed, Karrah?” Monika asks, looking across the room. Karrah nods with a grunt. “All closed up, as per usual,” she says. There’s a harshness to her voice that’s not usually there, even when she’s being the bouncer. “Good.” Monika twirls a shot glass between her fingers, then glances around at everyone and puts the glass away. She turns her serious look on you. “I’m glad you’re here, [pc.name]. Something’s come up, and you might be the only person we know who can help.” [pc.nmh |Whatever it is, you’ll be glad to help if you can. They’ve been good to you, and you’d like to return the favor. |You can’t promise anything, but you’ll listen, especially for the bar and the crew. Dhaal wouldn’t be the same without them. |They must be pretty desperate to come to you, but you’re here, so she can stop wasting your time and spit it out. ] Monika takes a deep breath. It looks like this is difficult for her to talk about. “About a day before Kiki messaged you,” she begins, “we got a distress call from our old crew.” Over by the door, Karrah snorts. Monika glances at her, but continues. “It’s from Redd, one of the other captains. After we ended up here thanks to what the Black Void did, Redd left, like most of the others. Last I heard, she’d found herself a new crew and somehow got hold of a ship, and was trying to go legit.” “Shipping’s good work if you can get it,” Josie adds, then smooths down the front of her apron. “At least, that’s what I heard at the dock back home. We didn’t really see any freighters.” Monika’s ears twitch toward Josie, then she continues. “But it looks like Redd ran into some trouble with her last run. Her distress call said something about sabotage, and a problem with some robots she was carrying.” Kiki shakes her head. “That’s a real easy way to get into trouble, carrying robots with any kind of guns or whatever. Someone decides they want to fuck you over, all they’ve got to do is hack into the bots, and suddenly they’ve got an army.” “That’s fucking cowardly,” Karrah mutters. “Take over the ship your damn self.” A faint smile flickers across Monika’s lips, then disappears. “It’s not as easy as Kiki makes it sound, but it could be that’s what happened.” She frowns, then looks away, and some of the sternness fades from her expression. “It’s been a long time since I’ve heard from Redd, since any of us have. If she reached out to me, she must be in serious trouble.” Karrah snorts, loud enough to echo in the concrete room. “Shows how much good going legit did her. Doesn’t she have some trader friends with a big fucking gunship by now? Maybe a merc group?” Monika narrows her organic eye at Karrah. “Do you have a problem with this, Karrah?” “She fucked off and left us here,” Karrah snarls. “You think she’d come for us if we sent her a distress call?” “She would,” Josie says, sincerity plain on her face. She clenches her hands into her milk-spotted apron, and looks more worried than you’ve ever seen her. “She absolutely would,” Monika says, staring down Karrah. “We all know what happened, no point in going over it again. But Redd’s still crew. And I don’t think for a second she wouldn’t come running to help us if we called her.” Karrah takes a deep breath and looks like she’s going to argue, then lets it out all at once. “Yeah, I know,” she grumbles, though she doesn’t look happy about it at all. “Wouldn’t be right to ignore her.” Monika gives Karrah a slow nod, then looks to Kiki. “Redd’s ship is a freighter, pretty standard model. Kiki?” Kiki fiddles with her glasses, and a holographic projection glows out of the round lens of her glasses. A blocky freighter ship appears in the air over the bar, bright blue, all hard lines and angles. The ship has two main sections, the rear larger than the front, with a narrow area in the middle and a triangular cockpit at the head. “Redd’s crew’s flying a Pyrite Industries Starhammer, nothing too special but it’s got a ton of cargo space. It’s a good ship for transport, mostly because the engine design means it won’t lose too much power or speed at heavier loads—” Monika clears her throat, and Kiki blushes a little, then continues without geeking out over the ship again. Josie giggles and whispers “loads” under her breath. “Anyway,” Kiki says, “we’ve got the coordinates for Redd’s ship, and the tracking info, so you can find it once you’re close. They call it the Mastodon.” She pauses, looks away for a moment, then continues. “We don’t know what you’ll find when you get there, because we haven’t heard from her since the first call.” She gives you a look up and down, but it feels more like she’s sizing you up than checking you out. “Hopefully it won’t be too bad, but I’m pretty sure you can handle some robots.” You ask if they think the Black Void is behind this, as that group was after them all before they split up. There’s a collective wince from the crew, and it’s a moment before anyone answers. “I hope not,” Monika says. “I can’t ask you to tangle with them. And if you show up and it looks like their work, I won’t blame you for taking off. But hopefully this is just some rival shipper trying to take out the competition.” “Or some major tech malfunction, or a stray asteroid that took out their shields, or something like that,” Kiki says quickly. She sounds nervous, and it seems like she’s trying to hide it by looking for the kinds of problems she can solve. “Don’t think we’re that lucky,” Karrah mutters, but says nothing more. “I just hope they’re okay,” Josie adds. “We all do,” Monika says. She gives you a considering look, fixing her natural eye on you. “So what do you say, [pc.name]? We’ve got no ship, and we can’t just bail out of here to come with you without risking losing the bar to some urban scavengers. You’re the only one who shows up here that might be able to handle whatever’s on that ship. Will you give us a hand with this?” "

rows.original: You tell the crew you’ll take the job. Monika and Kiki both start to say something, but they’re interrupted as Josie suddenly rushes across the bar. The cowgirl leans over the counter and pulls you into a hug, pressing your face right into her freckled cleavage. “Thank you,” Josie says, holding you in place and gently shaking you back and forth. “I was really worried. I kept thinking you’d say no, and then who would we ask? There’s maybe one other person who comes here who might be able to do this.” “She’s not wrong,” Kiki says, and when Josie finally releases you, you can see the concerned look on the blue-haired techie’s face. “This is probably going to be some heavy shit.” She smiles at you. “But I’m glad you’re up for it.” Josie giggles again at the phrasing, but Monika raises a hand before the cowgirl can say anything. “Thank you, [pc.name],” Monika says. “I don’t know if you’ve ever had a crew of your own, but if you have, you know what it’s like when one of them gets in trouble and needs a hand.” “Means you’re all in trouble, and it’s big damn heroes time,” Karrah says. She gives you an approving nod. “Wish I could come with you and bust some heads, but....” She glances back toward the bar’s door and shrugs. “We need you here, Karrah,” Monika says, though she’s wearing a small smile. Then, she turns her gaze on you. “Now let’s get you started. Kiki, send the coordinates to [pc.hisHer] codex.” “On it,” Kiki says, fiddling with the rim of her glasses again. “I’m jealous of that tech you got there, [pc.name],” she adds as she works. “I try to get a tap on everything that comes in here, because you never know if you’ll need to kick out a corp drone or get some blackmail material or whatever, but that thing? That was a surprise.” Not that it stopped her from hacking you, but at least she found it interesting. “I told you, your secret’s safe with us,” Kiki says, some teasing in her voice. “You know how this underground stuff works. We’re not going to sell you out while you’re scratching our backs... or is it....” “Let that one go, please,” Karrah says, holding a hand to her face. Kiki giggles, then gives her glasses a final tap. “Got it. I’ve sent you the coordinates for the ship, or at least where we think it is. It’s probably drifted some since the distress call, but I’m sure you can find it.” Monika nods to her, then gives you a serious look. “I know you’ve got other things going on, but I’d appreciate it if you could get out there soon,” she says. “All kinds of bad things can happen to a derelict ship, and Redd didn’t make it clear if they got out of there or not.” Put like that, it sounds pretty grim. You tell Monika you’ll get out there in good time. Next to her, Josie winces, curling her hands together in her apron. “Be careful out there, [pc.name]. If you can save the ship and the old crew, good, but don’t get yourself dead just for us.” You assure Josie you’ll stay as safe as you can. Handling this sort of thing is what being a rusher is all about. She doesn’t look convinced, but still gives you a smile. “Get word to us if you can, once you’ve found the ship and dealt with whatever’s happened to it,” Monika says. It seems like she’s holding her stern captain’s demeanor firmly in place, but you catch some quivering around her organic eye. This must mean a lot to her. Monika looks to the others, then says, “Let’s get this place open again. Karrah, walk [pc.himHer] out?” “Yeah,” Karrah says, and watches as you walk over to her. When you reach her, she gives you a punch on the shoulder that’s probably soft for her. You’ve taken lighter blows from some of the things you’ve fought. “Good to know you’re crazy enough to do this shit.” [pc.nmh|Helping people who need it isn’t crazy. It’s just the sort of thing you do. Especially for a crew who really needs the help.|Crazy? This is nothing. You two need to sit down with some drinks if she wants to hear about the really crazy stuff you’ve gotten up to.|This isn’t shit compared to some of the really heavy stuff you’ve done. You’d tell her, but then she’d just get jealous that none of her pirate days could ever compare.] Karrah just grunts as she leads you to the door, then looks [pc.heightRange 96|up|down] at you. “Don’t die,” she says, then bares her fangs in a grin. “I’d hate to never get hold of that ass again, and I’m not the only one.” The thraggen woman swats your [pc.ass] as she lets you out the door, and you head back into the abandoned Dhaal underground.
rows.translation: 你告诉船员们，自己会接下这份工作。 莫妮卡和琪琪同时开口，却被突然冲过酒吧的乔茜打断。牛女越过柜台俯身，把你拉进怀抱，将你的脸直接压进布满雀斑的乳沟。 “谢谢你，”乔茜说道，让你留在原地，轻轻前后摇晃。“我真的很担心。我一直在想，如果你拒绝了，我们还能去找谁？来这里的人里面，也许只有另外一个人可能做得到。” “她说得没错，”琪琪说道；乔茜终于放开你后，能看见蓝发技术员脸上担忧的神色。“这大概会是一件相当棘手的大事。”她向你微笑。“不过我很高兴你愿意做。” 乔茜再次因她的措辞咯咯笑起来，但莫妮卡抬手阻止牛女开口。“谢谢你，[pc.name]，”莫妮卡说道。“我不知道你是否拥有过自己的船员，但如果有过，就明白其中一人遇上麻烦、需要帮助时会是什么感觉。” “这意味着大家都遇上了麻烦，该到大英雄出场的时候了，”卡拉说道。她赞许地朝你点头。“真希望能和你一起去，打爆几个脑袋，可是...”她回头看了看酒吧门口，耸耸肩。 “我们需要你留在这里，卡拉，”莫妮卡说道，尽管脸上带着一丝微笑。随后，她把目光转向你。“现在，来帮你开始行动。琪琪，把坐标发到[pc.hisHer]法典里。” “马上，”琪琪说道，再次摆弄眼镜边缘。“我真嫉妒你手上的技术，[pc.name]，”她一边工作一边补充。“我会设法窃听进到这里的所有设备，因为你永远不知道什么时候需要赶走公司无人机，或者弄点勒索材料之类的；但那玩意？它真让我吃了一惊。” 当然，这也没能阻止她黑进你的设备，但至少她觉得它很有趣。 “我说过，你的秘密在我们这里很安全，”琪琪说道，声音里带着几分挑逗。“你知道地下生意怎么运作。你正帮我们抓背时，我们可不会出卖你...或者该叫...” “求你别再说这个了，”卡拉一手捂脸说道。 琪琪咯咯一笑，最后敲了一下眼镜。“搞定。我已经把飞船坐标发给你，或者至少是我们认为它所在的地方。发出求救信号后，它大概又漂移了一些距离，但我相信你能找到。” 莫妮卡朝她点头，随后严肃地望向你。“我知道你还有别的事情要做，但希望你能尽快赶过去，”她说道。“废弃飞船可能遭遇各种坏事，而且瑞德没说明她们是否已经逃离。” 这样一说，情况听起来相当严峻。你告诉莫妮卡，自己会及时赶到那里。 旁边的乔茜畏缩了一下，把双手蜷在围裙里。“在外面一定要小心，[pc.name]。如果能救下飞船和旧船员，那当然很好，但别仅仅为了我们把命丢掉。” 你向乔茜保证，会尽可能保障安全。应付这种事正是身为冲锋者的意义。她看起来没有被说服，但还是朝你微笑。 “如果可以的话，找到飞船并处理完那里发生的事后，给我们传个消息，”莫妮卡说道。她似乎正在竭力维持舰长的严厉态度，但你还是注意到生物眼睛周围略有颤抖。这件事对她一定意义重大。 莫妮卡望向其他人，随后说道：“让这里重新营业吧。卡拉，送[pc.himHer]出去？” “好，”卡拉说道，看着你走向她。你到达身旁后，她一拳砸在你肩上，这对她来说大概已经很轻柔。你战斗过的一些东西出手都没这么重。“很高兴知道你疯到足以干这种破事。” [pc.nmh|帮助有需要的人不叫疯狂。这只不过是你会做的事，尤其面对一群真的需要帮助的船员。|疯狂？这根本算不上什么。如果她想听你干过的真正疯狂事，你们两个得坐下来喝上几杯。|和你干过的一些真正棘手的事情相比，这根本算不上破事。你本来愿意讲给她听，可那只会让她嫉妒自己的海盗生涯完全无法相比。] 卡拉只是闷哼一声，领你走向门口，随后[pc.heightRange 96|抬头|低头]看着你。“别死了，”她说道，露出獠牙咧嘴一笑。“要是再也摸不到那个屁股，我会很难过；而且这么想的不止我一个。” 斯拉根女人放你出门时一巴掌拍在[pc.ass]上，你则重新走进废弃的达尔地下区域。

rows.original: [var0 |You fetch Paulette’s drawing and show it to Monika. “Do you know something about this logo?” The kaithrit barmaid squints, zooming in with her glowing blue eye. “I’ve seen it before, when we were looking for a place to open our bar. We didn’t stay long when Kiki looked into its tightly-locked intranet. You don’t wanna know what’s inside, trust me.” So she knows where it is? Monika nods. “Yes. It’s an abandoned factory at the far end of the Gyre — the last building before the sunward side of the city meets the sun-scarred steppes. Why do you want to go there?” “To help someone close,” you simply answer. “I see. There’s no reasoning with you then? They must be very important to be worth risking your life against experimental cyborgs and psycho warriors,” she says, reaching for her QComm-device. “Kiki? Can you come quickly? [pc.name] needs the E.G.G. data.” What was that about cyborgs and psionics? “Kiki will explain it better than I. The only thing I know is that the place drains huge amounts of energy from the power grid — a million times more than the bar does.” “Exactly 3.2 million times more,” Kiki adds before claiming the seat right next to you. “This isn’t your garden variety foundry, it’s a massive industrial complex. I’m surprised they don’t have their own reactor.” Sounds like the place isn’t as abandoned as it’s supposed to be. The dusky techie projects a 3D rendering of the E.G.G. on her holopad. “There’s only one entrance. It’ll surely be heavily guarded by a strong zaika — maybe XOs or something meaner. There’s been leaks in the ventilation system, lots of corridors are locked down, but the main rooms are still operational, according to the latest reports.” What can you expect inside? “Before they shut the factory down and purged the workers, they received a huge shipment of captured leyaks as well as a tanker full of chrome: segmented legs, sensors, targeting systems, drug injectors, monomolecular blades, and so on. The waiver also mentions a telepath mercenary — certainly a new manager or safety officer. The rest of the data was too heavily-encrypted to be cracked with my tools, but I have one last clue.” And it is? Kiki types something on the keyboard. A moment later, large tanks appear on screen. “There’s thousands of cryogenic chambers stored in the lowest level. I don’t know who or what they hold, but it can’t be good. Be careful [pc.name], you’re not dealing with a small fry.” “I will. Thank you Kiki — and you too Monika.” The [silly |milfy |mature ] kaithrit smiles. “It’s the least we can do after you brought the Mastodon back in one piece. I hope you’ll find what you’re looking for.” You have a hunch that you will. For now, Paulette will want to hear what you’ve learned. |You fetch Paulette’s drawing and show it to Monika. “Do you know something about this logo?” The kaithrit barmaid squints, zooming in with her glowing blue eye. “I’ve seen it before, when we were looking for a place to open our bar. rows.original: A cluster of Dhaal’s idle youth squat in a darkened alcove, hunched around something flickering and bluish. Looking closer, you discover a game of hardlight dice, though modified with projected obstacles and events to spice up the already competitive game. One young zaika doesn’t partake. Instead, she clutches a miniaturized projector in a hand laced with glowing circuitry. She must be running the game.
rows.translation: 一群无所事事的达尔年轻人蹲在昏暗的壁龛里，围着某个闪烁着蓝光的东西弓着身子。仔细一看，你发现那是一局硬光骰子游戏，只是额外加入了投影障碍和事件，让本就竞争激烈的游戏更加刺激。有个年轻的扎伊卡没有参与。相反，她紧握着一台微型投影仪，手上布满发光的电路纹路。游戏一定是由她主持的。
rows.raw: "A cluster of Dhaal’s idle youth squat in a darkened alcove, hunched around something flickering and bluish. Looking closer, you discover a game of hardlight dice, though modified with projected obstacles and events to spice up the already competitive game. One young zaika doesn’t partake. Instead, she clutches a miniaturized projector in a hand laced with glowing circuitry. She must be running the game."

rows.raw: "\n\nA large section of wall across the street from the youths is filled with half-scrapped mechanicals and other urban waste. The word ‘MOO’ is painted near it, in a curling script. As you walk past, you catch sight of a wide, arched doorway partly hidden behind the junk."

rows.original: The Crash Landing’s entry hall looks like it was once mostly concrete, but there are sheets of metal bolted across the walls now, along with steel beams holding up the ceiling. Some of them look supportive, others more decorative. Blue and yellow lights shine among all the metal, pulsing with the beat of the distant music. It’s dim, but not threatening, and promises a good time at the other end of the darkness.

rows.translation: 卡拉本人看起来百无聊赖，但她一只手搭在腰间的电击棍上注视着你，仿佛正等着已经进门的你做出什么举动。你可以找她聊聊，也可以径直去酒吧。
rows.raw: "\n\nKarrah herself looks bored, but watches you with one hand on the stun baton at her hip, like she’s waiting for you to make a move now that you’re inside. You could chat her up, or head for the bar."

rows.original: The Crash Landing’s entry hall looks like it was once mostly concrete, but there are sheets of metal bolted across the walls now, along with steel beams holding up the ceiling. Some of them look supportive, others more decorative. Blue and yellow lights shine among all the metal, pulsing with the beat of the distant music. It’s dim, but not threatening, and you know there’s a good time waiting at the other end of the darkness.
rows.translation: 迫降酒吧的入口大厅看起来原本大多由混凝土构成，但如今墙上钉满了金属板，天花板也由钢梁支撑。有些钢梁看起来确实用于承重，另一些则更像装饰。蓝色和黄色的灯光在金属之间闪耀，随着远处音乐的节拍脉动。这里很昏暗，却并不令人不安；你知道黑暗的另一端正有一场欢乐等着你。
rows.raw: "The Crash Landing’s entry hall looks like it was once mostly concrete, but there are sheets of metal bolted across the walls now, along with steel beams holding up the ceiling. Some of them look supportive, others more decorative. Blue and yellow lights shine among all the metal, pulsing with the beat of the distant music. It’s dim, but not threatening, and you know there’s a good time waiting at the other end of the darkness."

rows.original: The thraggen woman, Karrah, stands to one side, watching you from next to the enormous steel door she’s guarding. The familiar scanner unit is bolted to the wall next to her, so she can display herself outside the door. You remember what she said about stunners set up for security, and look up. Thin pipes run up and down the length of the ceiling, with mechanical stuff bolted onto them here and there. You’re not sure what most of it is, but there could be stunners in there somewhere.
rows.translation: 那名叫卡拉的特拉根女人站在一旁，守着身边那扇巨大的钢门，同时注视着你。熟悉的扫描装置固定在她旁边的墙上，让她能把自己的影像显示在门外。你想起她说过这里装有用于安保的电击器，便抬头望去。细管沿天花板纵横延伸，其间零零散散地固定着机械装置。你认不出其中大部分东西，但电击器很可能就藏在某处。
rows.raw: "\n\nThe thraggen woman, Karrah, stands to one side, watching you from next to the enormous steel door she’s guarding. The familiar scanner unit is bolted to the wall next to her, so she can display herself outside the door. You remember what she said about stunners set up for security, and look up. Thin pipes run up and down the length of the ceiling, with mechanical stuff bolted onto them here and there. You’re not sure what most of it is, but there could be stunners in there somewhere."

rows.original: Karrah herself looks bored,
rows.translation: 卡拉本人看起来百无聊赖，
rows.raw: "\n\nKarrah herself looks bored,"

rows.original: but watches you with one hand on the stun baton at her hip, like she doesn’t quite trust you.
rows.translation: 但她一只手搭在腰间的电击棍上注视着你，似乎还不怎么信任你。
rows.raw: " but watches you with one hand on the stun baton at her hip, like she doesn’t quite trust you."

rows.original: but she doesn’t keep her hand on her stun baton anymore, and she nods at you as your eyes meet. Looks like she knows you’re not here to start a fight.
rows.translation: 但她已经不再把手搭在电击棍上了；与你四目相对时，她向你点了点头。看来她知道你不是来惹事的。
rows.raw: " but she doesn’t keep her hand on her stun baton anymore, and she nods at you as your eyes meet. Looks like she knows you’re not here to start a fight."

rows.original: but seems relaxed around you, and gives you a smirk as your eyes meet. Looks like she knows you’re a regular customer and that the girls like you too.
rows.translation: 但她在你身边似乎很放松；与你四目相对时，她朝你得意一笑。看来她知道你是这里的常客，也知道姑娘们同样喜欢你。
rows.raw: " but seems relaxed around you, and gives you a smirk as your eyes meet. Looks like she knows you’re a regular customer and that the girls like you too."

rows.original: You could chat her up, or head for the bar.
rows.translation: 你可以找她聊聊，也可以径直去酒吧。
rows.raw: " You could chat her up, or head for the bar."

rows.original: Karrah
rows.translation: 卡拉
rows.raw: "Karrah"

rows.original: You walk into a large room with metal and concrete walls, lit by yellow and blue globes of light on the ceiling. The globes slowly fade from dim to brighter, making the room’s shadows fade and deepen in turn. Booths line the walls all around the room, filled with zaika in various levels of blissed-out on milk, talking and flirting and just sitting there staring at the lights. Hardlight displays and flickering monitors line the walls, showing news and sports and porn and whatever else the patrons want to see.
rows.translation: 你走进一间由金属和混凝土墙围成的大房间，天花板上的黄蓝色光球照亮四周。光球缓缓由暗转亮，让房内的阴影交替变淡、加深。墙边环绕着一圈卡座，里面坐满了因乳汁而陶醉程度不一的扎伊卡；她们有的交谈调情，有的只是坐着凝望灯光。硬光显示器和闪烁的屏幕铺满墙面，播放着新闻、体育、色情片，以及顾客想看的其他任何内容。
rows.raw: "You walk into a large room with metal and concrete walls, lit by yellow and blue globes of light on the ceiling. The globes slowly fade from dim to brighter, making the room’s shadows fade and deepen in turn. Booths line the walls all around the room, filled with zaika in various levels of blissed-out on milk, talking and flirting and just sitting there staring at the lights. Hardlight displays and flickering monitors line the walls, showing news and sports and porn and whatever else the patrons want to see."

rows.original: The bar sits at the back of the longest wall, a long steel horseshoe shape with about a dozen stools in front of it. More zaika sit on the stools, though some of them are swaying in place, their tails wrapped around the stools’ posts. Two women stand behind the bar, glasses in their hands as they work. One of them is a purple-haired kaithrit, and the other looks human but has bovine ears and a tail.
rows.translation: 酒吧位于最长那面墙的后方，是一座长长的钢制马蹄形吧台，前面摆着十来张高脚凳。更多扎伊卡坐在凳子上，其中一些还在原地摇晃，尾巴缠着凳腿。两名女人站在吧台后，手持酒杯忙碌着。其中一人是紫发凯瑟瑞特，另一人看起来像人类，却长着牛耳和牛尾。
rows.raw: "\n\nThe bar sits at the back of the longest wall, a long steel horseshoe shape with about a dozen stools in front of it. More zaika sit on the stools, though some of them are swaying in place, their tails wrapped around the stools’ posts. Two women stand behind the bar, glasses in their hands as they work. One of them is a purple-haired kaithrit, and the other looks human but has bovine ears and a tail."

rows.original: There’s a low rumble of conversation and laughter throughout the whole place, but at the same time, nobody really seems comfortable here. It feels like they know the bar is hidden for a reason, and with the stranglehold the corporations have on the city above, this place could get raided at any time just for being a different place to get milk. So it doesn’t look like anybody’s getting too wild, just drinking and trying to relax.
rows.translation: 整个地方都回荡着低沉的交谈声和笑声，但与此同时，似乎没有人真正感到自在。大家仿佛都明白这间酒吧之所以隐藏起来必有缘由；上方城市又被企业牢牢扼住，仅仅因为这里是另一个获取乳汁的地方，就可能随时遭到突袭。因此没有人玩得太疯，只是喝酒并试着放松。
rows.raw: "\n\nThere’s a low rumble of conversation and laughter throughout the whole place, but at the same time, nobody really seems comfortable here. It feels like they know the bar is hidden for a reason, and with the stranglehold the corporations have on the city above, this place could get raided at any time just for being a different place to get milk. So it doesn’t look like anybody’s getting too wild, just drinking and trying to relax."

rows.original: Another doorway opens to the west, rimmed with steel and lights glowing in all different colors. The pounding music is louder from that way, and through the doorway, you can see a dance floor filled with gyrating zaika, along with a pool table.
rows.translation: 另一扇门向西敞开，钢制门框边缘亮着五颜六色的灯。震耳的音乐从那边传来，声音更加响亮；透过门口，你能看到舞池里挤满了扭动身体的扎伊卡人，旁边还有一张台球桌。
rows.raw: "\n\nAnother doorway opens to the west, rimmed with steel and lights glowing in all different colors. The pounding music is louder from that way, and through the doorway, you can see a dance floor filled with gyrating zaika, along with a pool table."

rows.original: You could head to the bar and talk to one of the women there, or check out the dance and pool room.
rows.translation: 你可以去吧台找其中一名女人聊聊，也可以去看看舞厅和台球室。
rows.raw: "\n\nYou could head to the bar and talk to one of the women there, or check out the dance and pool room."

rows.original: You walk in to see the bar’s familiar metal and concrete walls, lit by yellow and blue globes of light on the ceiling. The globes slowly fade from dim to brighter, making the room’s shadows fade and deepen in turn. Booths line the walls all around the room, filled with the usual zaika in various levels of blissed-out on milk, talking and flirting and just sitting there staring at the lights. A few of them nod to you, recognizing that you’ve been here before. Hardlight displays and flickering monitors line the walls, showing news and sports and porn and whatever else the patrons want to see.

rows.original: You head into the bar’s next room, and a thumping bass line hits you right in the chest. There are some powerful speakers embedded in the walls here, lining the ceiling and behind grates near the floor. Flashing and fading lights of all colors and shapes shine from the walls, moving with the beat of the music, making the entire place feel like you’ve stepped into some kind of old-school club out of a rebellious science fiction novel.
rows.translation: 你走进酒吧的下一个房间，震耳的低音节拍迎面撞上胸膛。墙内嵌着一些功率强劲的扬声器，沿天花板排列，地板附近的格栅后也装着一排。各种颜色、各种形状的灯光在墙面上闪烁明灭，随着音乐节拍移动，让整个地方仿佛一间出自叛逆科幻小说的老派夜店。
rows.raw: "You head into the bar’s next room, and a thumping bass line hits you right in the chest. There are some powerful speakers embedded in the walls here, lining the ceiling and behind grates near the floor. Flashing and fading lights of all colors and shapes shine from the walls, moving with the beat of the music, making the entire place feel like you’ve stepped into some kind of old-school club out of a rebellious science fiction novel."

rows.original: Dozens of zaika shimmy and shake on the dance floor, a throbbing sea of sweaty bodies and shining hair and tails shivering back and forth. With the shifting lights and the dancing crowd, it’s hard to tell who’s where for more than a second or two, but everyone seems lost in the music, probably high on milk and glad for the chance to party.
rows.translation: 数十名扎伊卡在舞池中扭动摇摆，构成一片由汗湿躯体、闪亮头发和来回颤动的尾巴组成的起伏海洋。在变幻灯光与舞动人群之中，你很难连续一两秒看清谁在哪里；不过所有人似乎都沉浸在音乐中，大概正因乳汁而兴奋，也很高兴能有机会纵情狂欢。
rows.raw: "\n\nDozens of zaika shimmy and shake on the dance floor, a throbbing sea of sweaty bodies and shining hair and tails shivering back and forth. With the shifting lights and the dancing crowd, it’s hard to tell who’s where for more than a second or two, but everyone seems lost in the music, probably high on milk and glad for the chance to party."

rows.original: On the other side of the room stand two chunks of equipment with hardlight mounts on them. Whatever they once were, they’ve been jury-rigged into pool tables, with small hardlight projection rods hanging from the sides. A few zaika play pool at one table, using the hardlight rods as cues. Some other clearly-improvised hardlight projectors create dartboards on the walls, though there’s nobody playing there right now.
rows.translation: 房间另一侧立着两大块装有硬光支架的设备。不管它们原本是什么，如今都被临时改造成了台球桌，侧面悬着小型硬光投影杆。几名扎伊卡在其中一张桌边打球，把硬光杆当作球杆使用。另一些显然也是临时拼装的硬光投影仪在墙上生成飞镖靶，不过此刻没人玩飞镖。
rows.raw: "\n\nOn the other side of the room stand two chunks of equipment with hardlight mounts on them. Whatever they once were, they’ve been jury-rigged into pool tables, with small hardlight projection rods hanging from the sides. A few zaika play pool at one table, using the hardlight rods as cues. Some other clearly-improvised hardlight projectors create dartboards on the walls, though there’s nobody playing there right now."

rows.original: A human woman with skin about as dark as the zaika stands in one corner, watching over the place from behind a pair of glasses with mismatched lenses - one round, one rectangular. She’s wearing a dark purple vest and slacks that look like something from an old Earth movie, complete with a long-sleeved white shirt and a bowtie. The vest barely stays closed over her sizable chest. Her wavy blue hair trails down past her shoulders, and her eyes dart back and forth, like she’s trying to keep an eye on the whole room at once. Long, pointed ears stick out from beneath her hair.
rows.translation: 一名肤色与扎伊卡一样黝黑的人类女人站在角落，透过一副镜片不对称的眼镜观察全场——一边圆形，一边长方形。她穿着深紫色马甲和长裤，像是从地球老电影里走出来的一样，还搭配了长袖白衬衫与领结。马甲勉强包住她颇为丰满的胸部。波浪状蓝发垂过肩头，她的眼睛来回扫视，仿佛想同时照看整个房间。长而尖的耳朵从发丝下伸出。
rows.raw: "\n\nA human woman with skin about as dark as the zaika stands in one corner, watching over the place from behind a pair of glasses with mismatched lenses - one round, one rectangular. She’s wearing a dark purple vest and slacks that look like something from an old Earth movie, complete with a long-sleeved white shirt and a bowtie. The vest barely stays closed over her sizable chest. Her wavy blue hair trails down past her shoulders, and her eyes dart back and forth, like she’s trying to keep an eye on the whole room at once. Long, pointed ears stick out from beneath her hair."

rows.original: When the lights shift to shine on her, you catch sight of an enormous bulge between her legs. Whatever’s down there, she’s got a lot of it.
rows.translation: 灯光转到她身上时，你看见她双腿之间鼓起一大包。不管里面是什么，分量都相当惊人。
rows.raw: "\n\nWhen the lights shift to shine on her, you catch sight of an enormous bulge between her legs. Whatever’s down there, she’s got a lot of it."
