rows.original: In the kitchen there is a door styled to look like a cupboard, which leads onto a dimly lit corridor that adjoins all of the brothel’s rooms on this floor. Here the lavish artifice of the establishment falls away into racks of costumes, cluttered dressing tables, half-finished meals and overflowing ashtrays. Hard light posters and an automated PA issue soft but regular reminders to return to your room five minutes before your status is greenlit, that obedience and enthusiasm ensure avoiding demerits, and to ask your line manager about the affordable pleasure patch scheme. Deziere puts a finger to your lips and quickly and silently leads you through to a fire escape, plucking an access card out of her bosom to open it. Judging by the number of cigarette butts out here this metal balcony is a favourite amongst the employees, and why not: there’s a cool breeze almost free of artificial scent, and a fantastic view of the Gyre below. “Paragon bugs the prep area,” she says, lighting a cigarette. “But we should be able to talk here for a little while.” Bluish smoke billows from the chubby, robed kaithrit’s nose and lips, whipped away on the wind. She still talks the same way she always has to you, but her voice has lost the saccharine frosting it has when she’s coaxing you to let her feed or fuck you. “I suppose I always knew she’d come looking,” she says, gazing into the distance. “Nothing could ever get in the way of that girl, growing up.” She turns to look at you, her voice becoming thick. “How is Elizienne?” Elizienne? Oh Void. “No no Ms. d’Alysio, not that one,” you say. “Bizzy. Bizzy sent me.” “Bezeneria? But — she should be enjoying herself on that nature documentary shoot she told me about, not running around after me.” Worry has now edged into her raspy voice. She grasps your arm, hard. “Are you from the studio? Is my little Bizzy alright?” Oof. Ok, here goes. “No, Ms. d’Alysio. Or I guess I am from the studio. Kinda.” You cough. “Bizzy, uh... ran into difficulties. She reached out to me, and I... helped her.” You roughly outline how you came to own Bizzy, and the porn studio you built together. 德兹耶尔将一根手指贴在你唇上，迅速而无声地带你穿过走廊，来到消防通道。她从乳沟里抽出门禁卡，把门打开。从外面数量众多的烟蒂来看，这座金属阳台显然很受员工欢迎，而这毫不奇怪：这里吹着凉爽微风，几乎没有人造香味，脚下还能将环城的壮丽景色尽收眼底。 “典范公司在准备区装了窃听器，”她一边点烟一边说道。“不过我们应该能在这里谈一会儿。” 泛蓝烟雾从这个穿着长袍、身材丰满的凯斯里特鼻唇间涌出，随即被风卷走。她和你说话的方式依旧和从前一样，只是嗓音失去了哄你答应让她喂食或与你做爱时，那层糖霜般甜腻的修饰。 “我想，我一直知道她终有一天会来寻找，”她眺望远方，说道。“那姑娘从小到大，无论什么都挡不住她。”她转头看向你，嗓音变得哽咽。“艾丽茜恩过得怎么样？” 艾丽茜恩？哦，虚空啊。 rows.original: “Raskalia,” you mutter, letting your gaze drop. “That’s right. Raskalia. Who you need me to be.” She squeezes your hand; a quiet buzzing sound comes from somewhere. “Now let’s stop being silly and talk about you now, ok dumpling? That’s a much more important subject.” The kaithrit’s tone is brisk and lightly tinged with relief. You guess, if you want to broach the subject of who you think she really is, you’ll have to build up to it again. For now she’s Raskalia, an enjoyable treat that you’ve bought yourself. With a sigh, you begin to tell her about your day.
rows.translation: “拉斯卡莉娅，”你低声说道，垂下目光。 “没错。拉斯卡莉娅。你需要我成为的那个人。”她捏了捏你的手；不知何处传来轻微的嗡鸣。“现在别再犯傻了，聊聊你吧，好吗，小甜心？那才是重要得多的话题。” 凯斯里特的语气轻快，隐隐透着如释重负。你猜，如果还想提起你认为她真实身份为何的话题，就得重新慢慢铺垫。此刻她是拉斯卡莉娅，是你花钱为自己买下的一份愉悦享受。你叹了口气，开始向她讲述自己这一天。
rows.raw: " “Raskalia,” you mutter, letting your gaze drop. “That’s right. Raskalia. Who you need me to be.” She squeezes your hand; a quiet buzzing sound comes from somewhere. “Now let’s stop being silly and talk about you now, ok dumpling? That’s a much more important subject.” The kaithrit’s tone is brisk and lightly tinged with relief. You guess, if you want to broach the subject of who you think she really is, you’ll have to build up to it again. For now she’s Raskalia, an enjoyable treat that you’ve bought yourself. With a sigh, you begin to tell her about your day. "

rows.original: “What was I like when I was young?” A ghost of a smile appears on her round face, and she turns slightly in her chair to present the wide, form-dominating swell of her bosom to you. “Why, am I not good-looking enough for you now, cuddlebum? Did you want Dizzy when she could leap through parties and turn every head in the room? When her smile was fresh and she could touch her heels by bending over backwards?” “[pc.nmh |I’ve got Bizzy for that,” you grin, ogling her generous curves. “You’re good as you are.” |“Mmm, well maybe,” you grin, ogling her generous curves. “What I’m seeing now is a hell of a consolation prize.” |“Mmm, well maybe,” you grin, ogling her generous curves. “What I’m seeing now is a hell of a consolation prize.” ] Dizzy’s smile fades as her mind turns back. There’s a faint buzzing sound from the back of her head, and her expression grows calmer. “I guess I was pretty similar to you, sweetpea,” she says. “All I wanted when I was growing up was to get out into the galaxy and have as much fun as I possibly could. Except I didn’t come from anything special. My parents more or less kicked me out when I hit adulthood. So when things got... serious... I didn’t have anywhere to turn. No big space station nursery for Dizzy to put her kits in, and go back to bumming around the funnest parts of space.” She doesn’t say it with much bitterness; just a vague, misty sadness. “I could’ve dumped Zeddy with one of the corporations, you can do that if you’re from Rosha and a few other kaithrit colonies. But I remembered what it felt like to be unwanted. I never wanted a kit of mine to feel that way,” she says, tigerishness breaking through the misty melancholy. “So I settled on Gaerys, where they were advertising for workers. Not fun work, not high-paying work, but steady work, which is what you need when you’re raising one on your own.” “How did Lizzy and Bizzy come about?” you ask. She laughs awkwardly and sighs, twiddling a claw on the tabletop. “Dizzy was still pretty silly back then, honeybuns. But when someone as well paid as a Pyrite dock manager takes you as his girl, well, you start to dream, don’t you? Maybe life won’t always be as hard and dirty as it is on a hydro planet. And so maybe you ignore the warning signs, and what your friends are telling you, because that dream is too good to wake up from. I went into work one morning belly over my waistband with Bizzy and he was just... gone. I found out later his term on Gaerys had finished. He’d never meant to stick around, even after getting me pregnant twice.” She twists her needle claw back and forth on the table for a while. “And that’s why I don’t believe you about Bezeneria. Not until I see her.” She gives you that sad, vague smile. “Sorry blossom. Life’s knocked too many lessons into me.”
rows.translation: “我年轻时是什么样？”她圆润的脸上浮现一丝若有若无的微笑，身体在椅子上微微转动，将占据整副身形的宽阔饱满胸脯展示给你。“怎么，抱抱宝贝，我现在不够好看了吗？你想要的是那个能在派对间轻盈穿梭、让房间里所有人回头的迪兹？那个笑容还很清新，向后弯腰就能摸到脚跟的迪兹？” “[pc.nmh |那种事有比兹就够了，”你咧嘴笑着，目光贪婪地扫过她丰满的曲线。“你现在这样就很好。” |“嗯，也许吧，”你咧嘴笑着，目光贪婪地扫过她丰满的曲线。“不过眼前的景象也算是极佳的安慰奖。” |“嗯，也许吧，”你咧嘴笑着，目光贪婪地扫过她丰满的曲线。“不过眼前的景象也算是极佳的安慰奖。” ] 迪兹的笑容逐渐消失，思绪回到过去。她脑后传来轻微的嗡鸣声，神情也变得平静。 “我想，那时的我跟你很像，小甜心，”她说道。“成长过程中，我唯一想要的，就是闯进银河，尽可能玩个痛快。可我的出身并不特别。成年后，父母差不多就把我赶出了家门。所以等事情变得...严肃起来...我根本无处可去。没有一座大型太空站的育儿所能让迪兹寄放幼崽，再回到太空中最好玩的地方四处闲逛。” 她说这些话时并没有多少怨恨，只有一丝朦胧而遥远的悲伤。 “我本可以把泽迪送给某家公司。来自罗莎和另外几个凯斯里特殖民地的人都可以这么做。但我还记得自己不被需要是什么感觉。我绝不希望自己的孩子也有这种感受。”她说道，朦胧忧郁中透出母虎般的强硬。“所以我在盖里斯定居下来，那里当时正招工。工作既不好玩，薪水也不高，但胜在稳定，而独自抚养孩子最需要的就是稳定。” “那莉兹和比兹又是怎么来的？”你问道。她尴尬地笑了笑，叹息着，用一根爪尖在桌面上来回划弄。 “那时的迪兹还很傻，甜心宝贝。可当一个薪水丰厚的黄铁矿码头经理把你当作他的女人，你难免会开始做梦，对吧？也许生活不会永远像在水世界上那样艰难肮脏。于是你可能会无视那些警告信号，无视朋友们的话，因为那个梦实在太美好，让人不愿醒来。有一天早上，我挺着怀比兹的大肚子去上班，他却已经...走了。后来我才知道，他在盖里斯的任期已经结束。哪怕让我怀孕两次，他也从没打算留下。” 她用针状爪尖在桌面上来回划了好一阵。 “这就是我不相信你所说的贝泽妮莉娅近况的原因。除非亲眼见到她。”她向你露出那种悲伤而恍惚的微笑。“抱歉，小花。生活已经把太多教训硬塞进我脑袋里了。”

rows.original: Bizzy
rows.translation: 比兹
rows.raw: "Bizzy"

rows.original: “Oh, little Bezeneria. What a sweet thing she was when she was young. Never squawled like Zed did, never climbed onto the top of the shelves and sulked like Lizzy did.” Dizzy’s smile is wide and nostalgic. “She’d do anything her big brother and sister told her to. I had to stop her jumping into a turbine intake once. My word did Lizzy catch a spanking that time. I used to take her out to the river delta, where the marshlands are, and I think that’s where she was at her happiest, chasing about with her net and toy camera. When the mists rose you got so many rainbows...” “What was she like when she got older?” “Ants in her pants. They all did.” Dizzy laughs raspily, then sighs. “Who wouldn’t? Gaerys isn’t a place for a young person, unless they’re looking to disappear. Zed enlisted with the Confederate navy as soon as he was old enough and Lizzy, top marks in her class, got a good starter position with Pyrite. She wanted to track down her dad. Bezeneria though... she always had her head in the clouds. All those posters of extranet stars and celebrities, doing photo shoots of all her friends... she didn’t understand you don’t get to live that kind of life if you start where she did. And there’s so many people out there waiting to take what little you have for thinking that you can.” She chuckles a little again. “She didn’t even have... you know.” She makes round gestures in front of her. “The bigger you are as a female kaithrit, the more attractive. She wouldn’t even be able to make it as a gold digger, or a model. I worried about her so much.” “But you paid for her AV degree anyway.” “Yes, I did. With the bit of money I had saved, and the — loan. Carver type companies have fronts on every dead-end world like Gaerys, they know they’re full of poor suckers. I knew what it meant.” Her jaw is firm, but her tone is pleading. “But you’d do the same thing, wouldn’t you? I — my life was over by then, who cares what happens to this fat old bagpuss, but I could at least give my girl her dream. Just once, I wanted her to catch the rainbow.” Whirr goes the back of her head. She sighs again, long and heavy. “I guess there was still a little of silly, young Dizzy in me then. I should’ve made her stay and work. She would’ve learned better that way. But — I think she would’ve stopped being the Bizzy I loved so much then. The color would’ve washed out.”
rows.translation: “哦，小贝泽妮莉娅。她小时候真是个甜心。她从不像泽德那样号啕大哭，也不像莉兹那样爬到架子顶上生闷气。”迪兹露出开怀而怀念的笑容。“哥哥姐姐让她做什么，她都会照做。有一次，我不得不阻止她跳进涡轮进气口。天哪，那次莉兹可挨了一顿屁股。我以前常带她去河流三角洲，去那片湿地。我想，她在那里追着网和玩具相机到处跑的时候最快乐。雾气升起时，能看到那么多彩虹...” “她长大后是什么样？” “一刻都闲不住。他们几个都这样。”迪兹沙哑地笑了笑，随后叹息一声。“谁又能不这样？盖里斯不适合年轻人，除非他们想就此消失。泽德一到年龄就加入了邦联海军；莉兹则以全班最高分毕业，在黄铁矿工业找到了一份不错的入门职位。她想找到自己的父亲。可贝泽妮莉娅...她总是满脑子幻想。墙上贴满了外联网明星与名流的海报，还给所有朋友拍写真...她不明白，从她那样的起点出发，根本过不上那种生活。而外面有太多人等着利用你这种想法，把你仅有的一切也夺走。” 她又轻轻笑了一声。 “她甚至都没有...你知道的。”她在身前比画出圆润的形状。“雌性凯斯里特的身材越大，就越有吸引力。她连拜金女或模特都做不成。我那时实在太担心她了。” “但你还是替她支付了视听专业的学费。” “对，我付了。用我攒下的那点钱，还有那笔...贷款。卡弗之流的公司在盖里斯这种没有出路的世界到处设有门面，他们知道那里尽是穷困而好骗的人。我明白这意味着什么。”她绷紧下颌，语气却近乎恳求。“但你也会做同样的事，对不对？我、我的人生那时已经结束了，谁会在乎这个又老又胖的猫娘会落得什么下场？但至少我能把梦想交给女儿。哪怕只有一次，我也想让她抓住那道彩虹。” 她脑后传来嗡鸣声。她又长长地、沉重地叹了口气。 “我想，那时候我体内还残留着一点年轻愚蠢的迪兹。我本该强迫她留下工作。那样她就会得到更实际的教训。可是...我想，那样一来，她就不再是我深爱的比兹了。她身上的色彩会被冲洗干净。”

rows.original: Paragon
rows.translation: 典范
rows.raw: "Paragon"

rows.original: “So Carver indentured you after you couldn’t pay back the loan?” you say. “What was that like?” “I knew what was going to happen sweetpea, it wasn’t much of a shock.” Dizzy tucks a strand of white hair behind a triangular ear and smiles wryly. “I’d already done plenty of that type of work by then. Making the credits to raise three kids on your own isn’t a joke. It was the reason they were happy to take me on, despite my age. They put me in one of their orbital casinos, and honestly dear it was just a relief to get off Gaerys. There’s only so many shades of gray you can take.” “And I knew what I had to do.” She rearranges a stocking and snaps it with business-like emphasis. “Make friends with the other girls and boys who still have their minds, they’re the only ones who are going to look out for you. Endear yourself to the clients, so you become a favorite. Say no to the pleasure patches and stims, as tempting as they are. I got on fine, to begin with anyway. Really, the actual job — I liked it.” She shrugs her shoulders and smiles. “It’s more fun than being a space docker, let me tell you! I bring a little joy into people’s lives, there’s nothing wrong with that is there?” “To begin with?” you ask gingerly. “Well... even if you’re disciplined and a good earner, once a company like Carver’s has you, they keep you.” Twiddle twiddle, goes the claw on the table. “You gotta take boob-firming mods, or we’re transferring you to one of the really sleazy places. You gotta take anti-agathics, otherwise we’ll be knocking your price way down. The cost of those mods go on top of what you’re already paying back, with interest. You never leave, not until you’re completely used up or ready to be put into a fluid farm. I knew all that when I went to them, as I said. It was worth it, cherryblossom. [var0|You’re a parent, you understand right?|You’d know if you were a parent.]” “I did fight pretty hard not to be sent out here, though.” Just a trace of harsh bitterness in the pearly melancholy. “Paragon don’t allow indentured to communicate off-world, they don’t even want where they’re being sent to be known. And — talking with Bizzy from time to time was so important to me. But Carver wanted some of her best assets with Paragon to stake her claim here, ones that she thought could bring back clientele again and again, and how much do you think she cares that the asset in question doesn’t like it?” The rubenesque kaithrit shrugs at you, again with that wry, galaxy-weary smile. “So when I got angry about it they stuck an antenna in the back of my head that keeps me calm, took my tails away and shipped me out here anyway. And here I am, precious. That’s the story of Dizzy the fat dumb whore who failed every step of the way. Have you heard enough now?” Her fingers are flat and spread on the table, and she looks at you unsmiling. She really doesn’t want to talk any further.
rows.translation: “所以，你还不起贷款后，卡弗就让你签下契约服役？”你说道。“那是什么感觉？” “我知道会发生什么，小甜豆，所以并没有多震惊。”迪兹把一缕白发别到三角耳后，苦笑起来。“那时我已经做过很多这类工作。独自赚钱养大三个孩子可不是闹着玩的。尽管我年纪不小，他们仍乐意收下我，原因就在这里。他们把我安排进一座轨道赌场。老实说，亲爱的，能离开盖里斯本身就让我松了口气。一个人能忍受的灰暗色调终究有限。” “而且我知道自己该做什么。”她重新整理一只丝袜，像处理公事般用力弹了一下。“和那些还保有心智的姑娘与男孩交朋友，他们才是唯一会照应你的人。讨客人喜欢，好让自己成为宠儿。快乐贴片与兴奋剂再诱人也要拒绝。最初我过得还不错。说真的，那份工作本身，我挺喜欢。”她耸耸肩，露出微笑。“这可比当太空码头工有趣多了，我跟你说！我给人们的生活带来一点快乐，这没什么不对，是吧？” “最初？”你小心翼翼地问。 “嗯...就算你守规矩又会赚钱，一旦落进卡弗这种公司的手里，他们就会一直攥着你。”桌上的爪尖来回划弄。“你必须接受坚挺乳房的改造，否则我们就把你调去那些真正肮脏的场所。你必须使用抗衰老药，否则我们就大幅压低你的价码。这些改造的费用会连本带利地叠加到原有欠款上。你永远别想离开，除非被彻底榨干，或者已经可以送进体液农场。我说过，去找他们时，我就知道这一切。这是值得的，小樱桃。[var0|你也是父母，应该能够理解，对吧？|如果你当过父母，自然就会明白。]” “不过，为了不被送来这里，我确实拼命抗争过。”珍珠般朦胧的哀伤中，透出一丝尖锐的苦涩。“典范公司不许契约奴与外星联系，甚至不愿让外界知道他们被送到哪里。而且，偶尔和比兹聊聊对我实在太重要了。可卡弗想把手中最好的几项资产送给典范，好在这里占下一席之地；她要的是那些能让客人一次次回来的资产。你觉得她会在乎那项资产本人乐不乐意吗？” 这个身材丰腴如画中美人的凯斯里特又朝你耸了耸肩，脸上依然挂着那种看透银河的苦笑。 “所以，我为这件事发火后，他们就在我后脑装了一根让我保持平静的天线，夺走我的尾巴，照样把我运来这里。于是我就在这里了，宝贝。这就是又胖又蠢的妓女迪兹一路步步失败的故事。现在你听够了吗？” 她把手指平展着摊在桌上，面无笑容地看着你。她真的不愿再继续谈下去了。
rows.raw: " “So Carver indentured you after you couldn’t pay back the loan?” you say. “What was that like?” “I knew what was going to happen sweetpea, it wasn’t much of a shock.” Dizzy tucks a strand of white hair behind a triangular ear and smiles wryly. “I’d already done plenty of that type of work by then. Making the credits to raise three kids on your own isn’t a joke. It was the reason they were happy to take me on, despite my age. They put me in one of their orbital casinos, and honestly dear it was just a relief to get off Gaerys. There’s only so many shades of gray you can take.” “And I knew what I had to do.” She rearranges a stocking and snaps it with business-like emphasis. “Make friends with the other girls and boys who still have their minds, they’re the only ones who are going to look out for you. Endear yourself to the clients, so you become a favorite. Say no to the pleasure patches and stims, as tempting as they are. I got on fine, to begin with anyway. Really, the actual job — I liked it.” She shrugs her shoulders and smiles. “It’s more fun than being a space docker, let me tell you! I bring a little joy into people’s lives, there’s nothing wrong with that is there?” “To begin with?” you ask gingerly. “Well... even if you’re disciplined and a good earner, once a company like Carver’s has you, they keep you.” Twiddle twiddle, goes the claw on the table. “You gotta take boob-firming mods, or we’re transferring you to one of the really sleazy places. You gotta take anti-agathics, otherwise we’ll be knocking your price way down. The cost of those mods go on top of what you’re already paying back, with interest. You never leave, not until you’re completely used up or ready to be put into a fluid farm. I knew all that when I went to them, as I said. It was worth it, cherryblossom. [var0|You’re a parent, you understand right?|You’d know if you were a parent.]” “I did fight pretty hard not to be sent out here, though.” Just a trace of harsh bitterness in the pearly melancholy. “Paragon don’t allow indentured to communicate off-world, they don’t even want where they’re being sent to be known. And — talking with Bizzy from time to time was so important to me. But Carver wanted some of her best assets with Paragon to stake her claim here, ones that she thought could bring back clientele again and again, and how much do you think she cares that the asset in question doesn’t like it?” The rubenesque kaithrit shrugs at you, again with that wry, galaxy-weary smile. “So when I got angry about it they stuck an antenna in the back of my head that keeps me calm, took my tails away and shipped me out here anyway. And here I am, precious. That’s the story of Dizzy the fat dumb whore who failed every step of the way. Have you heard enough now?” Her fingers are flat and spread on the table, and she looks at you unsmiling. She really doesn’t want to talk any further. "

rows.original: “Tell me about your mods,” you say. “Did Paragon give you all of them?” “No, Carver gave me a couple, back before she subcontracted me.” She cups the vast, dumpling-like swells of her breasts, lifts them up a bit, and then lets them fall. Though tides of plump flesh ripple mesmerically across them, they retain a perkiness that suggests silicone. But they are entirely real, a joy to sink your hand into. “Aren’t they nice?” she beams. “Memmory Gland is heaven-sent for older girls like me. And I was given a round of anti-agathics, so I will look like this for a good twenty years yet.” Her smile turns sadder. “Which is just as well, because I will be paying them off with my ass for about half that length of time. Freezing time isn’t cheap.” “Carver prefers gene mods... and Paragon prefers synthetics I guess,” you supply, gazing down at her tails. She brings the two dark gray appendages snaking upwards, deftly twirls their smooth heft around each other into a helix. “They’re cutting edge apparently. Supposed to show off how skillful and sexy their implants can be. I do miss my old tails sometimes, but the fluff can be so annoying to comb and these are a lot of fun, I have to admit. I can get up to all sorts with them.” You reach out and, when she doesn’t pull them away, stroke one of them, reaching your grip around its warm, smooth heft, observing the pleasure in the kaithrit’s emerald’s eyes and the scratchy purr which starts up in the back of her throat. “And the... sticks?” you say, turning your gaze up to her head. The two four inch long synthetic twigs crossed together beneath her hair bun appear to be a decorative tie at first glance, but up close you can see they’re actually fused to her scalp[flags.DIZZY_ANAL|...or if you happen to have given them a good tug in the heat of things.] “They’re, um... antenna, sugarsnap. Connected to my spinal cord. They do a few things.” She laughs self-consciously, shifting in her seat. “They identify the species of my clients right away and download dietary information, so I’m never in danger of poisoning anyone. I just look at someone and woosh, my head’s just filled with food suggestions and warnings! Very useful if you like cooking as much as me. They’re also, um... sensitive. More so than my tails. Paragon love giving their employees extra erogenous zones I guess, they certainly do a good job keeping ol’ Dizzy’s engine turning over, no matter how many clients she’s seen to in a day.” She twirls her hair embarrassedly. “Do they do anything else?” you say. [flags.DIZZY_TALK_PARAGON|“You said something about keeping you sedate.”] “They... make the bad feelings go away,” she says at last. She gathers her formidable self up and suddenly frowns at you furiously. There’s a familiar buzzing sound, and the frown melts away into placidity. “I used to get very sad when I... thought about things, and sometimes very angry. Now, when I feel those emotions building up inside me, I feel the hum, and then they dissipate. I can still remember everything, but it’s like a... sea, great and gray, instead of a geyser, rising up.” “How do you feel about that?” “How would I be able to tell?” She gives you that wry, world-weary smile. “I... think I don’t mind it? I like being able to stay calm and collected, it helps a lot with my job, and... feeling sexy and smart is good. But I don’t like Paragon being inside my head. I don’t like that they control even how I feel about how they own me.” The plump kaithrit touches one of the blunt little antennae, and murmurs as sensation sweeps down her neck. “But we all have to play with the hand we got dealt don’t we, sunbeam? There are boys and girls working in this place who’ve gotten their brains swirled around way, way worse than me.”
rows.translation: “跟我说说你身上的改造吧，”你说道。“它们全都是典范公司给你装的吗？” “不是，在把我的契约转包出去以前，卡弗给了我几项。”她双手托住自己那两团硕大、犹如饺子般鼓胀的乳房，将它们稍稍抬起，然后任其落下。丰腴的肉浪在上面迷人地荡漾开来，可它们依然坚挺得让人以为里面填了硅胶。但它们完完全全是真的，手掌陷进去时，触感令人愉悦。 “很不错吧？”她喜气洋洋地说道。“对我这种年纪不小的姑娘来说，‘乳忆腺’简直是上天的恩赐。我还接受了一轮抗衰老药治疗，所以至少未来二十年，我都会保持现在这副模样。”她的笑容染上一丝哀伤。“这样也好，毕竟为了还清这笔钱，我大概要用自己的屁股接客，花上差不多一半那么长的时间。冻结岁月可不便宜。” “卡弗更喜欢基因改造...而典范公司大概更偏爱合成植入体，”你接话道，目光落向她的尾巴。她让两条深灰色的附肢蜿蜒上探，灵巧地将光滑而沉甸甸的尾身彼此缠绕成螺旋状。 “听说它们采用了最尖端的技术，应该是用来展示他们的植入体能有多精巧、多性感。我有时确实会怀念以前的尾巴，可蓬松的毛梳起来实在烦人，而且我不得不承认，这两条尾巴很好玩。我能用它们做各种各样的事。” 你伸出手；见她没有把尾巴缩回去，便抚摸起其中一条，用手握住温暖、光滑而沉甸甸的尾身。凯斯里特那双翡翠色眼眸中流露出的愉悦，以及从喉咙深处响起的沙哑呼噜声，都被你尽收眼底。 “那这些...棍子呢？”你说道，将目光转向她的头顶。两根四英寸长的合成细枝交叉在她的发髻下，乍看像是装饰性的发簪，但凑近后，你便能看出它们其实与她的头皮融为一体[flags.DIZZY_ANAL|...当然，如果你在激情正酣时用力拽过它们，你早就知道了。] “它们是，呃...天线，小甜脆豆。和我的脊髓相连。它们有好几种功能。”她有些难为情地笑了笑，在座位上挪动着身体。“它们能立刻识别客人的种族，下载相应的饮食资料，这样我就永远不会不小心让谁中毒。我只需看一个人一眼，嗖的一下，脑袋里就会装满食物建议和警告！如果你和我一样喜欢烹饪，那可非常实用。它们还，呃...很敏感，比我的尾巴还敏感。我想典范公司就是喜欢给员工增添新的性感带。他们确实很会让老迪兹的引擎一直运转，无论她一天伺候了多少客人都一样。”她尴尬地绕弄着自己的头发。 “它们还有别的功能吗？”你问道。[flags.DIZZY_TALK_PARAGON|“你刚才说过，它们能让你保持镇静。”] “它们...会让那些糟糕的情绪消失，”她终于说道。她挺起自己魁梧的身躯，忽然怒气冲冲地瞪向你。一阵熟悉的嗡鸣声响起，那副怒容随即化为平静。“以前，每当我...思考某些事情，就会变得非常难过，有时还会非常愤怒。如今，当我感觉那些情绪在体内越积越多时，就会感受到那阵嗡鸣，随后情绪便消散了。我依然记得一切，可那感觉像是一片...广阔而灰暗的海，不再像喷泉般向上喷涌。” “你对此有什么感受？” “我怎么可能分辨得出来？”她露出那种嘲谑而饱经世故的笑容。“我...想我并不介意？我喜欢自己能够保持冷静沉着，这对工作很有帮助，而且...感觉自己既性感又聪明也挺好。可是，我不喜欢典范公司侵入我的脑袋。我不喜欢他们甚至能控制我该如何看待他们占有我这件事。”这名丰腴的凯斯里特轻触一根钝圆的小天线，感官刺激掠过颈项，令她低声呻吟。“不过，我们都只能打好命运发到手里的牌，不是吗，小阳光？在这个地方工作的男孩女孩里，有些人的脑子被搅弄得比我严重太多、太多了。”

rows.original: The Future
rows.translation: 未来
rows.raw: "The Future"

rows.original: “Where do you see yourself in the future?” you ask. “Sweetpea, don’t ask me that.” the kaithrit laughs raspily, her bosom quivering, eyes turned away from you. “I’ve told you everything there is to know about me, you know I don’t have a future. I’ll be working here until I can’t anymore, and then I’ll be thrown on a trash heap. When I lose myself in the job, just focus on making people happy, and having fun myself... that’s when I’m at my happiest.” “Don’t say that,” you say. “You must have a dream of something beyond this.” “You’re so young and sweet.” She smiles at you sadly. “I learned not to hope for anything for myself a long time ago, and that way I’ve never been disappointed. Dreams were for young, silly Dizzy. She’s gone now.” “But if you’re asking what she dreamt of...” She sighs, slit pupils dilating a bit. “...She liked making food, she always did, and maybe she thought about being a professional cook one day. Or being a teacher, looking after little ones, maybe she thought she’d be good at that. She even looked at getting a qualification, before Lizzy came along.” Her needle claw has left a lot of interesting little patterns on the tabletop. “That was all a very long time ago. Think about your own future [pc.name], not mine.”
rows.translation: “你觉得自己将来会是什么样？”你问道。 “小甜心，别问我这个。”凯斯里特沙哑地笑起来，胸脯微微颤动，目光转向一旁。“关于我的一切，我都已经告诉你了。你知道我没有未来。我会一直在这里工作，直到再也干不动，然后被扔进垃圾堆。我全身心投入工作，只想着让别人开心、也让自己找点乐子的时候...才是我最幸福的时候。” “别这么说。”你说道。“除了这里，你一定也梦想过别的生活。” “你真年轻，也真可爱。”她悲伤地朝你微笑。“很久以前，我就学会了不为自己抱任何希望。这样一来，我也就从不会失望。梦想属于年轻又傻气的迪兹。她如今已经不在了。” “不过，要是你问她曾经梦见过什么...”她叹了口气，竖瞳微微放大。“...她喜欢做饭，一直都喜欢。也许她想过有朝一日成为职业厨师。或者去当老师，照顾小孩子；也许她觉得自己很适合。莉兹出现以前，她甚至研究过要去考个资格证。”她的针爪已经在桌面上留下许多有趣的小图案。“那都是很久以前的事了。想想你自己的未来吧，[pc.name]，别想我的。”

rows.original: With the casual flourish worthy of a bigshot mining magnate, you produce your codex and prep your account for a large transfer. Schraesta tips the flat screen to you, where a green tick sits below Deziere d’Alysio’s personal file and a long string of legalese. After a slight pause, you press your finger onto the tick. You now own Dizzy. “The asset will be sent securely to your spacecraft — she’ll be waiting for you there. Now, will you satisfy my curiosity, Captain Steele?” The expensively garbed zaika bends the screen back to her and fixes a pair of slightly bemused artificial eyes on you. “There are far sprightlier and more intriguing assets available here — and you could have bought them for far cheaper at source. Instead you’ve come up here to pay over the odds for this overweight, ageing alien. Why?”
rows.translation: 你带着大矿业巨头才有的随意气派取出电子法典，让账户准备好进行一笔大额转账。施雷斯塔把平板屏幕斜向你，上面在德齐耶尔·达利西奥的个人档案和一长串法律术语下方显示着一个绿色勾号。稍作停顿后，你将手指按在勾号上。现在，迪兹归你所有了。 “这件资产会被安全送到你的飞船——她将在那里等你。现在，你能满足一下我的好奇心吗，斯蒂尔船长？”身穿昂贵服饰的扎伊卡人把屏幕弯回自己面前，用一双略显困惑的人造眼睛盯着你。“这里有远比她更活泼、更有趣的资产——而且你本可以在源头用便宜得多的价格买下她们。可你偏偏来到这里，为这个肥胖衰老的外星人支付远高于市价的钱。为什么？”

rows.original: “Fuck you, and fuck this whole place.” Schraesta’s ears stand on end and her eyes widen, but she sits in stunned silence as you go on. “What you and that disgusting piece of trash you call Carver did to Dizzy turns my stomach, and I know that behind every door in this place there’s a story just like it. I have to get her back to her family, which is just as well, because right now I want to grind this business beneath my boot, starting with you and this office. You can tell both of your bosses I said that.” Without another word you sweep from the Peer’s office and head back down to the ground floor. Saying that felt better than any orgasm you could’ve paid for here.
rows.translation: “去你妈的，也去这整个鬼地方的。”施雷斯塔的耳朵猛然竖起，双眼睁大，可当你继续说下去时，她只是震惊地沉默坐着。“你和那个被你称作卡弗的恶心垃圾对迪兹做的事，让我反胃。我知道，这地方每扇门后都有一个相同的故事。我必须把她送回家人身边，这正合我意，因为现在我恨不得把这门生意踩在靴底碾碎，就从你和这间办公室开始。你可以把这番话转告给你的两个老板。” 你不再多说一个字，径直走出同僚的办公室，返回底层。说出这些话，比在这里花钱买到的任何高潮都更加痛快。

rows.original: “That’s my own business,” you reply, maintaining a neutral expression. “I have my reasons for wanting her, and they led me to negotiating this deal with you. I’m glad we didn’t come to blows over it, and that you believe it was good business.” “I — of course, Captain Steele!” Schraesta says, slightly flustered. “I respect your professionalism, and your desire for confidentiality. Any time, I’m sure...” “Good day.” You rise from your seat, sweep from her office to the elevator and head back down to the ground floor, thoughts already turning to the chubby package being delivered to [pc_ship.theName].
rows.translation: “那是我自己的事。”你面无表情地回答。“我有想要她的理由，正是这些理由让我来找你谈成这笔交易。我很高兴我们没有因此动手，而你也认为这是一桩好生意。” “我——当然，斯蒂尔船长！”施雷斯塔略显慌乱地说道。“我尊重你的专业态度，也尊重你对保密的要求。以后随时都可以，我相信...” “再会。” 你从座位起身，快步离开她的办公室，搭乘电梯返回底层，思绪已经转向那个即将被送到[pc_ship.theName]的丰满包裹。

rows.original: “You seem surprised, Peer. It made perfect sense to me,” you say, leaning back in your chair with an air of casual largesse. “I needed an experienced asset at my own operation. You had an older pro on your books weighing you down. And, if it was a pricey deal... that’s alright, isn’t it? Steele Tech and Paragon are practically partners at this point.” You give her a wink. “I think giving you a small cash injection is a good investment for the future.” “Of course, Captain Steele! Suits you!” Schraesta is all smiles. “Practically partners... yes, it all makes perfect sense, of course. Isn’t it wonderful when interests align and business runs as smoothly as this? Please, whenever you’re in the area or indulging downstairs, please come up. There’s plenty of other matters we could turn our attention to.” You grip her hand and then return to the elevator. You gaze down at the hedonistic carnival as you descend back into it. You could build something similar one day for yourself, if you set your will to it.
rows.translation: “你似乎很惊讶，主管。但在我看来，这再合理不过了，”你说着，带着一副漫不经心又出手阔绰的气派靠回椅背。“我自己的产业需要一名经验丰富的人才，而你们账上有个上了年纪的老手，正拖累你们。就算这笔交易价格高昂...也没关系，不是吗？斯蒂尔科技和典范现在几乎就是合作伙伴。”你朝她眨眨眼。“我认为，给你们注入一小笔资金，是一项着眼未来的好投资。” “当然，斯蒂尔船长！真有您的风格！”施雷斯塔笑逐颜开。“几乎是合作伙伴...没错，一切当然都合情合理。各方利益一致，生意又运转得如此顺畅，岂不是妙极了吗？以后只要您来到附近，或者在楼下寻欢，请务必上来坐坐。还有许多其他事务，值得我们共同关注。” 你握了握她的手，随后返回电梯。电梯载着你降回那片纵欲的嘉年华时，你低头俯瞰着它。只要下定决心，将来有一天，你也能为自己建造一处类似的地方。

rows.raw: "You aren’t interested in seeing Dizzy, you’re interested in buying her outright. Who do you have to talk to to make that happen?"

rows.original: “You. Sweetpea.” The chubby kaithrit takes a sharp step towards you, raises her hand and then halts, eyes wide, her usually soft expression tight with emotion. She looks unsure what to say or do. “They — they put this collar on me and told me my contract had been bought, but they wouldn’t say by who,” Dizzy says, grip digging into the Paragon rainproof thrown over her shoulders. “I did think — but usually when that happens it’s by big shot pirates or execs for private collections, and so — but it’s you.” She stares at you plaintively. “Why?” You weren’t willing to bring Bizzy to this snakepit of a planet to see her, so you’re doing the next best thing: you’re bringing her to see Bizzy. Buying her out was a necessity in order to fulfill your promise. Dizzy starts to cry, inky mascara crawling silently down her round cheeks. She fumbles around in her chemise and dabs at the damage with a crumpled up tissue. “The antenna was supposed to stop these sorts of dreams,” she mumbles, turning her wet marble eyes up to the pink-tinted Dhaal sky. “They’re worse than anything else.” “It’s not a dream. Look.” You step into her and give her a firm hug, pressing yourself into the pillowy give. “Doesn’t that feel real? You’re my employee now. And if there’s one thing I can promise, I’m not Beth Carver.” After a moment she squeezes you back, nestles her face in your shoulder and sobs a couple of times. “I’m sorry,” she sniffs, breaking away to brush at her rapidly-dissolving make-up again. “It’s — this is just the nicest thing anyone’s ever done for me.” “C’mon,” you smile at her, nodding at the boarding ramp. “Let’s get you onboard.” Dizzy will remain on your ship until the next time you visit Bizzy.
rows.translation: “你。小甜豆。” 胖乎乎的凯斯里特朝你猛迈一步，抬起手，却又停住了。她睁大双眼，平时温柔的表情因强烈情绪而绷紧，看起来不知该说什么、做什么。 “他们——他们给我戴上这个项圈，说我的契约已经被人买下，却不肯告诉我买家是谁，”迪兹说道，手指深深攥进披在肩上的典范防雨衣。“我确实想过——但这种事通常都是有权有势的海盗或高管为了私人收藏而做的，所以——可竟然是你。”她神情凄楚地凝视着你。“为什么？” 你不愿意把比兹带到这个蛇窟般的星球来见她，所以决定退而求其次：把她带去见比兹。为了兑现承诺，把她买下来是必须的。 迪兹哭了起来，墨色睫毛膏悄无声息地沿圆润脸颊往下淌。她手忙脚乱地从衬裙里摸出一团皱巴巴的纸巾，擦拭花掉的妆。 “天线本来应该阻止这种梦的，”她喃喃自语，抬起湿润如大理石般的眼睛，望向染着粉色的达尔天空。“这种梦比其他一切都更糟。” “这不是梦。你看。”你上前一步，用力抱住她，把自己压进她枕头般柔软的身体。“感觉不像真的？你现在是我的雇员了。而且我至少可以保证一件事：我不是贝丝·卡弗。” 片刻之后，她也用力抱住你，把脸埋进你的肩头，抽泣了几声。 “对不起，”她吸着鼻子，松开怀抱，再次擦拭迅速化开的妆容。“只是——这是有生以来别人为我做过最美好的事。” “来吧，”你朝她微笑，向登船坡道点了点头。“我们上船。” 迪兹将留在你的飞船上，直到你下次去见比兹。

rows.original: Her body is thin and wiry, but rather than appearing frail, you get the impression of surprising strength being compacted into her diminutive form. Her chest is on the smaller side, and can’t be much larger than a B-cup, while the line of her waist and hips is visible but not too pronounced. Though her body isn’t as traditionally curvy as most other women’s, her face is unmistakably feminine. The girlishness of her features stand out even without any makeup.
rows.translation: 她身材纤瘦精悍，却并不显得虚弱，反而让你觉得这娇小身躯里凝聚着惊人的力量。她胸部偏小，顶多只有B罩杯，腰臀线条虽能看出，却不算突出。尽管她的身体没有大多数女性那种传统意义上的玲珑曲线，面容却无疑十分女性化。即使不施粉黛，五官中的少女感也格外鲜明。

rows.original: Her jacket is made of a tough, leathery looking material, colored a surprisingly soft shade of mauve. Though cropped at the waist, its sleeves are full length, albeit pushed up to just below her elbows. It features a stiff, wide collar that juts straight up. The entire jacket itself is covered in various zippered pockets, big and small. They look like they’re filled with all sorts of useful things. Underneath the jacket is a charcoal-colored v-neck t-shirt.
rows.translation: 她的夹克由坚韧、皮革般的材质制成，颜色却是出人意料的柔和淡紫红色。衣摆短至腰间，袖子却是长袖，只是被推到了肘部下方。宽阔硬挺的衣领笔直竖起。整件夹克上布满大小不一的拉链口袋，看起来装着各种实用物件。夹克里面是一件炭灰色V领T恤。

rows.original: Her pants are made of black leather and skintight, held in place with a pair of overlapping belts, one of which hangs a little more loosely on her hip than the other. On the upper belt hangs a series of pockets and various tools, much like how her jacket seems to be stuffed with goodies. A third belt encircling her leg is equipped with a holster containing a large pistol. The right leg of her pants has been cropped short to show off a sliver of thigh, only for the rest of the limb to be covered by a thigh-high stocking. Both feet are laced up in well-worn combat boots with a sensible inch-high heel.

rows.original: Evening shrugs, before slumping low against the bar. She crosses her arms and sighs pensively. “It’s a number of different things. For one, I never got an apprenticeship, which means I don’t have an established merc’s name that I can throw around for clout. When you’re first starting, there’s a lot of people claiming to be trained by so-and-so or this guy or that, one of the bigger, badder mercs already in the game. It’s enough to get you the edge over another beginner when it comes to getting picked. That, and a lot of potential hirers tend to balk when they see I’m ‘just a human’. They can’t help but think I’ll be out-run, out-muscled, or out-smarted by the next merc over. To be honest, I wouldn’t blame them... a lot of times it turns out to be true.”
rows.translation: 伊芙宁耸耸肩，随即伏低身子靠在吧台上。她抱起双臂，若有所思地叹了口气。“原因很多。首先，我从没拜过师，这意味着我没有哪位成名佣兵的名号可以拿来给自己撑场面。刚入行时，很多人都会声称自己受过某某人的训练，不是这个就是那个，反正都是业内更有名、更厉害的佣兵。挑人时，光凭这点就足以让你压过另一个新人。此外，许多潜在雇主一看我‘只是个人类’，往往就会打退堂鼓。他们总觉得，旁边随便一个佣兵都能跑得比我快、力气比我大或脑子比我聪明。说实话，我也不能怪他们...很多时候事实的确如此。”

rows.original: The woman shakes her head sadly, a short ‘tsk’ sucked through her teeth. “It’s not all bad, though. There’s something to be said for being underestimated. And I’ve got some skills of my own; I don’t mean to brag, but I’m a pretty good fucking shot,” the mercenary says, none too smugly. “As in, put a bullet through a moving target’s eyeball with a hand cannon while they’re jet-packing through the air a hundred meters away kind of good. Sometimes you don’t need to be smarter or stronger than someone. Just fast enough to get the drop on them, or prepared enough to outplan them. And if you’re in a pinch, weeellll, explosions always help.”
rows.translation: 女人伤感地摇摇头，牙缝间轻轻吸出一声‘啧’。“不过，也不全是坏事。被人低估自有被低估的好处。而且我也有自己的本事；不是我吹牛，我他妈枪法相当准，”佣兵说道，语气丝毫不显自满。“准到能在一百米外，用手炮一枪打穿一个正背着喷气背包飞行的移动目标的眼珠。有时你不必比别人聪明或强壮，只需出手快到能抢占先机，或准备充分到能在计划上胜过对方。真到了紧要关头，嗯，爆炸永远有用。”

Sometimes you don’t need to be smarter or stronger than someone. Just fast enough to get the drop on them, or prepared enough to outplan them. And if you’re in a pinch, weeellll, explosions always help.”"

rows.original: “So what kinds of clients do take you on?”
rows.translation: “那么究竟什么样的客户才会雇你？”
rows.raw: "\n\n“So what kinds of clients do take you on?”"

rows.original: “Uggggggggh, the worst ones.” Evening throws her head back with a groan. “My rates are dirt cheap, so I get picked up for the smallest bullshit sometimes. Like being a bodyguard for some rich asshole at a party. Or murdering some rich asshole’s relative- spoiler alert, not how mercenaries work. Or standing guard on some rich asshole’s pleasure yacht so he can carry on what I think was an affair, except it was with a sex doll.”
rows.translation: “呃啊啊啊啊啊，最糟的就是这种。”伊芙宁仰头呻吟。“我的收费便宜得要命，所以有时会接到些鸡毛蒜皮的破事。比如在派对上给某个有钱混蛋当保镖。或者去杀某个有钱混蛋的亲戚——先剧透一下，佣兵可不是这么干活的。又或者守在某个有钱混蛋的享乐游艇上，让他继续一场我以为是偷情的事，结果对象居然是个性爱娃娃。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Uggggggggh, the worst ones.” Evening throws her head back with a groan. “My rates are dirt cheap, so I get picked up for the smallest bullshit sometimes. Like being a bodyguard for some rich asshole at a party. Or murdering some rich asshole’s relative- spoiler alert, not how mercenaries work. Or standing guard on some rich asshole’s pleasure yacht so he can carry on what I think was an affair, except it was with a sex doll.”"

rows.original: You’re starting to see a pattern with where she’s going.
rows.translation: 你渐渐看出了她这番话的规律。
rows.raw: "\n\nYou’re starting to see a pattern with where she’s going. "

rows.original: “So, yeah, sometimes it’s weird, and sometimes it’s petty as fuck. Usually both. At least they’re mostly easy jobs, and occasionally I get to do something fun, like defend a ship against a bunch of manic cross-planet racers.”
rows.translation: “所以嘛，有时候很怪，有时候又他妈小家子气。通常两样都占。至少大多数活儿都挺轻松，偶尔我还能碰上点有意思的，比如保护一艘船，抵御一群疯狂的跨星球赛车手。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“So, yeah, sometimes it’s weird, and sometimes it’s petty as fuck. Usually both. At least they’re mostly easy jobs, and occasionally I get to do something fun, like defend a ship against a bunch of manic cross-planet racers.”"

rows.original: “You’re not too picky,” you observe.
rows.translation: “你不怎么挑剔。”你评价道。
rows.raw: "\n\n“You’re not too picky,” you observe."

rows.original: “Nah, as much as I’d like to be. I have family back home on Terra, so I usually take every job I can get and send a good chunk of what I make to them.”
rows.translation: “是啊，尽管我很想挑剔一点。我在泰拉老家还有家人，所以我通常能接什么活就接什么，再把挣来的很大一部分寄给她们。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Nah, as much as I’d like to be. I have family back home on Terra, so I usually take every job I can get and send a good chunk of what I make to them.”"

rows.original: “You have family?”
rows.translation: “你还有家人？”
rows.raw: "\n\n“You have family?”"

rows.original: The woman nods, a hint of pride in her features. “A sister with two little daughters. She’s pregnant with a third.”
rows.translation: 女人点点头，神情中带着一丝自豪。“我有个姐姐，她有两个年幼的女儿，现在还怀着第三个。”
rows.raw: "\n\nThe woman nods, a hint of pride in her features. “A sister with two little daughters. She’s pregnant with a third.” "

rows.original: You’re curious to see what they look like. “Any pictures?” you ask. However, just as you press the subject, Evening’s smile falters before fading away entirely. A tense silence lingers a little too long between the two of you.
rows.translation: 你很好奇他们长什么样。“有照片吗？”你问。然而就在你追问时，伊芙宁的笑容一滞，随后彻底消失。你们之间的紧张沉默持续得有些太久。
rows.raw: "\n\nYou’re curious to see what they look like. “Any pictures?” you ask. However, just as you press the subject, Evening’s smile falters before fading away entirely. A tense silence lingers a little too long between the two of you."

rows.original: When she answers, it’s barely aloud, in a shameful mutter. “No.” She takes a furtive sip from her glass. More silence.
rows.translation: 她回答时声音几乎低不可闻，羞愧地嘟囔道：“没有。”她偷偷抿了一口杯中的酒。又是一阵沉默。
rows.raw: "\n\nWhen she answers, it’s barely aloud, in a shameful mutter. “No.” She takes a furtive sip from her glass. More silence."

rows.original: Oh. Oh no. You’ve stumbled on a sore spot that maybe you shouldn’t have touched. Perhaps it’s time to change the subject...
rows.translation: 哦。糟了。你碰到了一个也许不该触碰的痛处。或许该换个话题了...
rows.raw: "\n\nOh. Oh no. You’ve stumbled on a sore spot that maybe you shouldn’t have touched. Perhaps it’s time to change the subject..."

rows.original: Herself
rows.translation: 她自己
rows.raw: "Herself"

rows.original: Herself
rows.translation: 她自己
rows.raw: "Herself"

rows.original: Ask Evening about herself.
rows.translation: 问问伊芙宁自己的事。
rows.raw: "Ask Evening about herself."

rows.original: Dhaal
rows.translation: 达尔
rows.raw: "Dhaal"

rows.original: You ask her what she thinks of Dhaal, since you get the feeling that she’s new to the planet as well.
rows.translation: 你问她对达哈尔有什么看法，因为你觉得她似乎也是刚来这颗星球。
rows.raw: "You ask her what she thinks of Dhaal, since you get the feeling that she’s new to the planet as well."

rows.original: “New enough,” she agrees. “I came here a few weeks ago, and I like it so far. Big city? Constant action? A place where evening literally reigns?” The pun that’s barely a pun earns a
rows.translation: “确实挺新鲜，”她赞同道。“我几周前才来这里，目前感觉还不错。大城市？时时刻刻都有事情发生？一个真正由夜晚统治的地方？”这个几乎算不上双关的双关让你发出
rows.raw: "\n\n“New enough,” she agrees. “I came here a few weeks ago, and I like it so far. Big city? Constant action? A place where evening literally reigns?” The pun that’s barely a pun earns a"

rows.original: politely stifled sigh
rows.translation: 被礼貌压下的叹息
rows.raw: " politely stifled sigh"

rows.original: quiet boo
rows.translation: 轻声的嘘声
rows.raw: " quiet boo"

rows.original: frustrated groan
rows.translation: 沮丧的呻吟
rows.raw: " frustrated groan"

rows.original: from you, which the eponymous woman pretends not to hear. “I almost feel like this place was made for me. Not bad at all for a Rush planet, eh? Plus, there’s a lot of work to be had here, what with the civil unrest. Riots, dissidents, all that.”
rows.translation: ，而这位与其同名的女人假装没有听见。“我几乎觉得这里就是为我量身打造的。对一颗大开拓时代的星球来说，相当不错，对吧？再说，这里有大量工作可接，毕竟社会动荡不断。暴乱、异见分子，诸如此类。”
rows.raw: " from you, which the eponymous woman pretends not to hear. “I almost feel like this place was made for me. Not bad at all for a Rush planet, eh? Plus, there’s a lot of work to be had here, what with the civil unrest. Riots, dissidents, all that.”"

rows.original: Hold on. “Are you working for the zaibatsu?” you ask in hushed tones. Karrah made it pretty clear that they weren’t welcome in The Crash Landing.
rows.translation: 等等。“你在为财阀工作吗？”你压低声音问道。卡拉已经说得很清楚，坠落点不欢迎他们。
rows.raw: "\n\nHold on. “Are you working for the zaibatsu?” you ask in hushed tones. Karrah made it pretty clear that they weren’t welcome in The Crash Landing."

rows.original: Evening shakes her head. “Nah, corpos won’t touch me,” she says with a tut. “Their loss. No, I’m more of a... freelancer.” Her head jerks almost imperceptibly towards a pair of zaika sitting in a corner, dressed in gang colors. “There’s plenty of other people here that could use a helping hand: impassioned activists, gang members, even the occasional ordinary joe getting terrorized by one of the above. Those poor bastards.” The look on her face conveys a sense of pity, but not that much pity. “Point is, I’m willing to hear all of their problems out, for a price.”
rows.translation: 伊芙宁摇摇头。“不，那些公司根本不肯碰我，”她咂嘴说道。“是他们的损失。不是，我更像是个...自由职业者。”她的头几乎难以察觉地朝角落里两个身穿帮派色服装的扎伊卡偏了一下。“这里还有很多别的人用得上帮手：热血上头的活动人士、帮派成员，甚至偶尔还有被前两者之一吓得不轻的普通人。那些可怜的混蛋。”她脸上流露出几分同情，但也没多同情。“重点是，只要价钱合适，我愿意听他们所有人的难题。”
rows.raw: "\n\nEvening shakes her head. “Nah, corpos won’t touch me,” she says with a tut. “Their loss. No, I’m more of a... freelancer.” Her head jerks almost imperceptibly towards a pair of zaika sitting in a corner, dressed in gang colors. “There’s plenty of other people here that could use a helping hand: impassioned activists, gang members, even the occasional ordinary joe getting terrorized by one of the above. Those poor bastards.” The look on her face conveys a sense of pity, but not that much pity. “Point is, I’m willing to hear all of their problems out, for a price.”"

rows.original: Speaking of the zaika, you ask what she thinks of them. It’s not every day a new, civilized species emerges.
rows.translation: 说到扎伊卡人，你问她怎么看这个种族。一个新的文明种族可不是每天都会出现。
rows.raw: "\n\nSpeaking of the zaika, you ask what she thinks of them. It’s not every day a new, civilized species emerges."

rows.original: To this question, your conversation partner cocks her head to the side. “I’m not sure yet. I’ve been watching them for a while, but I definitely haven’t seen enough to understand all of their culture – their customs, their quirks, and all that. They’re obsessed with some things I’ll never see the appeal of.” She swishes her glass, filled with the cream liquor usually more favored by the natives of the planet than a human like her. “I guess ‘do as the Romans do’ can’t really apply when the Romans are literal aliens. I will say I don’t appreciate getting jumped by a milk thief every time I step outdoors.” She gestures to her small bust, rolling her eyes. “Dumbasses think I’m lactating with a chest like this? And by the time I get them to knock it off, they end up begging me to fuck them afterwards. Every time. Even though I never do.”
rows.translation: 听见这个问题，与你交谈的女人把头偏向一边。“我还不确定。我观察他们有一阵子了，但看到的肯定还远远不够，没法理解他们文化的方方面面——他们的习俗、怪癖，诸如此类。他们痴迷的一些东西，我永远也看不出有何吸引力。”她晃了晃酒杯，里面装着这种星球原住民通常比她这样的人类更青睐的奶油利口酒。“我想，罗马人都成了货真价实的外星人，‘入乡随俗’这句话也没法真正适用了。我必须说，每次出门都被偷奶贼袭击，实在令人不爽。”她指了指自己平坦的胸部，翻了个白眼。“那些蠢货看见这么点胸，居然以为我在产奶？等我终于让他们住手，他们之后又会求我操他们。每次都这样，哪怕我从来没答应过。”
rows.raw: "\n\nTo this question, your conversation partner cocks her head to the side. “I’m not sure yet. I’ve been watching them for a while, but I definitely haven’t seen enough to understand all of their culture – their customs, their quirks, and all that. They’re obsessed with some things I’ll never see the appeal of.” She swishes her glass, filled with the cream liquor usually more favored by the natives of the planet than a human like her. “I guess ‘do as the Romans do’ can’t really apply when the Romans are literal aliens. I will say I don’t appreciate getting jumped by a milk thief every time I step outdoors.” She gestures to her small bust, rolling her eyes. “Dumbasses think I’m lactating with a chest like this? And by the time I get them to knock it off, they end up begging me to fuck them afterwards. Every time. Even though I never do.”"

rows.original: “How come?”
rows.raw: "\n\n“How come?”"

rows.original: You’re met with a shrug and a sigh. “I’m just not up for it,” Evening says, the weariness in her voice palpable. “Call it my ‘delicate Terran sensibilities’ coming through, but something about having to beat someone into submission before they proposition me really kills my boner.”
rows.translation: 回应你的是一声叹息和耸肩。“我就是提不起兴致，”伊芙宁说道，语气中的疲惫清晰可闻。“就当是我那‘娇贵的地球人感性’在作祟吧，但非得先把谁揍到屈服，对方才来向我求欢，这事真的让我彻底软了。”
rows.raw: "\n\nYou’re met with a shrug and a sigh. “I’m just not up for it,” Evening says, the weariness in her voice palpable. “Call it my ‘delicate Terran sensibilities’ coming through, but something about having to beat someone into submission before they proposition me really kills my boner.” "

rows.original: She pauses. “Metaphorically.”
rows.translation: 她顿了一下。“我是打个比方。”
rows.raw: "\n\nShe pauses. “Metaphorically.”"

rows.original: Dhaal
rows.translation: 达尔
rows.raw: "Dhaal"

rows.original: Dhaal
rows.translation: 达尔
rows.raw: "Dhaal"

rows.original: Ask her how she likes Dhaal as a fellow newcomer.
rows.translation: 问问同为新来者的她喜不喜欢达哈尔。
rows.raw: "Ask her how she likes Dhaal as a fellow newcomer."

rows.original: Hobbies
rows.translation: 爱好
rows.raw: "Hobbies"

rows.original: You ask her what her favorite hobbies are.
rows.translation: 你问她最喜欢哪些兴趣爱好。
rows.raw: "You ask her what her favorite hobbies are."

rows.original: “Guns,” she announces, almost instantaneously.
rows.translation: “枪。”她几乎不假思索地宣布。
rows.raw: "\n\n“Guns,” she announces, almost instantaneously."

rows.original: “Guns?” you ask.
rows.translation: “枪？”你问道。
rows.raw: "\n\n“Guns?” you ask."

rows.original: “Guns,” she affirms. “I didn’t always have a thing for them, but I warmed up to them real well. It was just when I started out as a mercenary – I’d bought what looked like a good pistol and was practicing with it for the first time. It was an eagle handgun, nothing fancy, but heavier than I thought it would be. Heavy, and loud, and a little scary, if I’ll be honest. I didn’t have anyone to show me the ropes, so I had to learn how to use it by myself. One day, I was practicing, and I happened to have an apple on hand. Out of curiosity, I threw it into the air and took a shot at it.” Evening mimes the action, complete with sound effects. “Bullet went straight through.”
rows.translation: “枪，”她肯定地说。“我并非一直喜欢枪，只是后来慢慢喜欢得不得了。那是在我刚当上佣兵的时候，我买了一把看起来不错的手枪，第一次拿它练习。那是把鹰式手枪，没什么花哨的，但比我预想的更沉。又沉、又响，说实话还有点吓人。没人教我入门，所以只能自己摸索怎么用。有一天我练枪时，手边正好有个苹果。出于好奇，我把它抛到空中，对着它开了一枪。”伊芙宁连声音效果都一并模仿，表演出整套动作。“子弹直接穿了过去。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Guns,” she affirms. “I didn’t always have a thing for them, but I warmed up to them real well. It was just when I started out as a mercenary – I’d bought what looked like a good pistol and was practicing with it for the first time. It was an eagle handgun, nothing fancy, but heavier than I thought it would be. Heavy, and loud, and a little scary, if I’ll be honest. I didn’t have anyone to show me the ropes, so I had to learn how to use it by myself. One day, I was practicing, and I happened to have an apple on hand. Out of curiosity, I threw it into the air and took a shot at it.” Evening mimes the action, complete with sound effects. “Bullet went straight through.”"

rows.original: You whistle in surprise. “You were that good straight off the bat?”
rows.translation: 你惊讶地吹了声口哨。“你一上手就这么厉害？”
rows.raw: "\n\nYou whistle in surprise. “You were that good straight off the bat?”"

rows.original: “That’s pretty sweet,” you contemplate, “but was it on purpose?”
rows.translation: “那可真酷，”你琢磨道，“不过那是故意的吗？”
rows.raw: "\n\n“That’s pretty sweet,” you contemplate, “but was it on purpose?”"

rows.original: “Hmm,” you hum in contemplation. “Lucky shot?”
rows.translation: “嗯，”你若有所思地哼了一声。“蒙中的？”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Hmm,” you hum in contemplation. “Lucky shot?”"

rows.original: The woman snorts. <i>“
rows.translation: 女人嗤笑一声。<i>“
rows.raw: "\n\nThe woman snorts. <i>“"

rows.original: You guessed it.
rows.translation: 被你猜中了。
rows.raw: "You guessed it."

rows.original: Hell no!
rows.translation: 绝对不行！
rows.raw: "Hell no!"

rows.original: My eyes were closed! I was lucky I didn’t accidentally shoot anyone. Still one of the coolest things to ever happen to me. I told myself I was gonna pull it off again, on purpose next time, no matter what. Years later, here I am. A really good fucking shot, and plenty comfortable with guns. I have a whole collection and everything!”
rows.translation: 我当时闭着眼睛！没误伤到人纯属走运。可那仍是我经历过最酷的事之一。我告诉自己，无论如何都要再来一次，下次得有意做到。多年以后，我成了现在这样。枪法他妈的准得很，玩枪也得心应手。我甚至还有一整套收藏！”
rows.raw: " My eyes were closed! I was lucky I didn’t accidentally shoot anyone. Still one of the coolest things to ever happen to me. I told myself I was gonna pull it off again, on purpose next time, no matter what. Years later, here I am. A really good fucking shot, and plenty comfortable with guns. I have a whole collection and everything!”"

rows.original: “A collection? How big is it?”
rows.translation: “收藏？有多大规模？”
rows.raw: "\n\n“A collection? How big is it?”"

rows.original: “Mmm, nothing crazy. It’s mostly pistols, a few rifles, a submachine gun or two. I even got a literal cannon from a job way back when. It’s a shame that I never find a good time and place to use it, but that’s okay; some of my guns are to use, some I’m tinkering with to bring them to working order, and some of them are just... nice to have.” Evening closes her eyes momentarily, reminiscing about various gun-related memories. She seems to enter a state of great peace and contentment that you only recall seeing on the faces of particularly religious men. Or stoned ones. Or quite possibly both.
rows.translation: “嗯，没什么太夸张的。主要是手枪，还有几把步枪和一两把冲锋枪。我甚至在很久以前的一份工作中弄到过一门真正的大炮。可惜一直找不到合适的时间和地点使用，不过也无所谓；我的枪有些用来射击，有些正由我摆弄着修复到可用状态，还有些只是...摆在那里就让人开心。”伊芙宁短暂闭上眼睛，回味着各式与枪有关的记忆。她似乎进入了一种极为安宁满足的状态，你只记得在特别虔诚的人脸上见过这种神情。或者嗑嗨了的人。又或者很可能两者兼有。
rows.raw: "\n\n“Mmm, nothing crazy. It’s mostly pistols, a few rifles, a submachine gun or two. I even got a literal cannon from a job way back when. It’s a shame that I never find a good time and place to use it, but that’s okay; some of my guns are to use, some I’m tinkering with to bring them to working order, and some of them are just... nice to have.” Evening closes her eyes momentarily, reminiscing about various gun-related memories. She seems to enter a state of great peace and contentment that you only recall seeing on the faces of particularly religious men. Or stoned ones. Or quite possibly both."

rows.original: Eventually she opens her eyes, her fantasizing over. “Other than that... I wouldn’t say I get up to anything special. It’s kinda hard for me to keep up regular hobbies when I spend so much time traveling to different places. Although I suppose that could count as a hobby all on its own.”
rows.translation: 最终她睁开眼睛，结束了遐想。“除此之外... 我也不会说自己有什么特别的消遣。我花了太多时间四处旅行，很难维持固定爱好。不过我想，旅行本身也能算一种爱好。”
rows.raw: "\n\nEventually she opens her eyes, her fantasizing over. “Other than that... I wouldn’t say I get up to anything special. It’s kinda hard for me to keep up regular hobbies when I spend so much time traveling to different places. Although I suppose that could count as a hobby all on its own.”"

rows.original: Hobbies
rows.translation: 爱好
rows.raw: "Hobbies"

rows.original: Hobbies
rows.translation: 爱好
rows.raw: "Hobbies"

rows.original: What does she like to do in her free time?
rows.translation: 她空闲时喜欢做什么？
rows.raw: "What does she like to do in her free time?"

rows.original: Mods
rows.translation: 身体模组
rows.raw: "Mods"

rows.original: You tell Evening that you’re curious; if she thinks she’s falling behind in the mercenary game because of the stiff competition, why doesn’t she use any mods to even out the playing field?
rows.translation: 你告诉伊芙宁你有点好奇：如果她觉得自己因为竞争激烈而在佣兵行业里逐渐落后，为什么不用点改造来拉平差距？
rows.raw: "You tell Evening that you’re curious; if she thinks she’s falling behind in the mercenary game because of the stiff competition, why doesn’t she use any mods to even out the playing field?"

rows.original: The woman in question stops short, eyebrows shooting upwards. She clearly was not expecting you to ask that. “Uhhhh...”
rows.translation: 被问到的女人猛然停住，眉毛高高扬起。她显然完全没料到你会这么问。“呃...”
rows.raw: "\n\nThe woman in question stops short, eyebrows shooting upwards. She clearly was not expecting you to ask that. “Uhhhh...”"

rows.original: Oops, looks like you caught her off guard.
rows.translation: 哎呀，看来你问得她措手不及。
rows.raw: " Oops, looks like you caught her off guard."

rows.original: Deer in headlights, thy name is Evening.
rows.translation: 像只被车灯照住的鹿，而她的名字就叫伊芙宁。
rows.raw: " Deer in headlights, thy name is Evening."

rows.original: What, has she literally never considered it before?
rows.translation: 怎么，她难道真的从来没想过？
rows.raw: " What, has she literally never considered it before?"

rows.original: Eventually, the mercenary throws up her hands as if to placate some unknown assailant, or quell an argument that has yet to happen. Looks like this isn’t her first time talking about this, and that similar, previous encounters didn’t exactly pan out well for her.
rows.translation: 最后，这名佣兵举起双手，像是在安抚某个看不见的袭击者，又或是在平息一场尚未发生的争论。看来她不是第一次谈这件事，而过去类似的交谈显然并不愉快。
rows.raw: "\n\nEventually, the mercenary throws up her hands as if to placate some unknown assailant, or quell an argument that has yet to happen. Looks like this isn’t her first time talking about this, and that similar, previous encounters didn’t exactly pan out well for her."

rows.original: Wanting to understand her perspective a bit more, you ask Evening to explain again why she’s so against using mods.
rows.translation: 为了多理解一点她的想法，你请伊芙宁再解释一次，她为什么如此反对使用改造物。
rows.raw: "Wanting to understand her perspective a bit more, you ask Evening to explain again why she’s so against using mods."

rows.original: She doesn’t look as caught off guard as the first time you asked her, but the purse of her lips indicates that it’s still a complicated question for her to answer.
rows.translation: 她不像你第一次问时那样措手不及，但抿起的嘴唇表明，这对她来说依然是个很难回答的问题。
rows.raw: "\n\nShe doesn’t look as caught off guard as the first time you asked her, but the purse of her lips indicates that it’s still a complicated question for her to answer."

rows.original: “Look, don’t get me wrong, I have nothing against other people using them. You wanna give yourself bat wings, tentacles, hell, even a new dick, go ahead; I wouldn’t stop you. But personally, I think they come with a lot of risks. I’d rather not take them myself if I can help it.”
rows.translation: “听着，别误会，我不反对别人用改造。你想给自己装蝙蝠翅膀、触手，见鬼，就算换根新鸡巴也随你；我不会拦着。但就我个人而言，我觉得风险太多。能不碰的话，我宁愿自己不用。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Look, don’t get me wrong, I have nothing against other people using them. You wanna give yourself bat wings, tentacles, hell, even a new dick, go ahead; I wouldn’t stop you. But personally, I think they come with a lot of risks. I’d rather not take them myself if I can help it.”"

rows.original: You ask her exactly what she means.
rows.translation: 你问她具体是什么意思。
rows.raw: "\n\nYou ask her exactly what she means. "

rows.original: “Well, let me answer your question with another question,” the woman proposes. “If you changed everything about yourself, would you cease to exist?”
rows.translation: “这样吧，让我用另一个问题回答你的问题。”女人提议道。“如果你改变了自己的一切，你还会继续存在吗？”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Well, let me answer your question with another question,” the woman proposes. “If you changed everything about yourself, would you cease to exist?”"

rows.original: You half pout, half frown. That’s a really hard sounding question, and you are so not about to think that much. “What kind of question is that, silly?”
rows.translation: 你半撅嘴、半皱眉。这问题听起来实在太难了，你才不要费那么多脑筋。“这是什么问题呀，笨蛋？”
rows.raw: "\n\nYou half pout, half frown. That’s a really hard sounding question, and you are so not about to think that much. “What kind of question is that, silly?”"

rows.original: Your brows furrow as you try to mull the question over. Your mind turns up blank. “Run that by me again, bro?”
rows.translation: 你皱紧眉头，试图仔细思考这个问题，脑中却一片空白。“老兄，再说一遍？”
rows.raw: "\n\nYour brows furrow as you try to mull the question over. Your mind turns up blank. “Run that by me again, bro?”"

rows.original: You frown. “What kind of question is that?”
rows.translation: 你皱起眉。“这算什么问题？”
rows.raw: "\n\nYou frown. “What kind of question is that?”"

rows.original: You frown. “What do you mean?”
rows.translation: 你皱起眉。“你是什么意思？”
rows.raw: "\n\nYou frown. “What do you mean?”"

rows.original: “I mean, if you dyed your hair, replaced your eyes, switched your species, and then took a drug that completely rewired your brain, would you even be the same person anymore? Think about it.” She taps the side of her head with a finger. “Every part of you would have been replaced. Transformatives these days can even scramble your DNA if you’re not careful. So if all of those things happen, can you prove that you’re the same person you were before changing? I know it’s a silly thing to worry about,” Evening admits, “but I feel like if you were to do that, it’d mean erasing your existence altogether. I don’t want to take that chance and wake up one day realizing my old self has disappeared. It feels like... dying, in a way.”
rows.translation: “我的意思是，如果你染了头发，换掉眼睛，改变种族，再吃下一种彻底重塑大脑的药，你还能算原来的那个人吗？仔细想想。”她用一根手指点点太阳穴。“你的每一部分都被换掉了。如今的转化物稍不留神甚至会打乱你的DNA。那么，如果这一切都发生了，你能证明自己仍是改变前的那个人吗？我知道担心这种事很傻，”伊芙宁承认道，“但我觉得真那么做，就等于彻底抹掉自己的存在。我不想冒这个险，在某天醒来后发现过去的自己已经消失了。某种意义上，那感觉就像...死亡。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“I mean, if you dyed your hair, replaced your eyes, switched your species, and then took a drug that completely rewired your brain, would you even be the same person anymore? Think about it.” She taps the side of her head with a finger. “Every part of you would have been replaced. Transformatives these days can even scramble your DNA if you’re not careful. So if all of those things happen, can you prove that you’re the same person you were before changing? I know it’s a silly thing to worry about,” Evening admits, “but I feel like if you were to do that, it’d mean erasing your existence altogether. I don’t want to take that chance and wake up one day realizing my old self has disappeared. It feels like... dying, in a way.”"

rows.original: The mercenary exhales heavily, now rubbing at her temples. “I know that puts me at a disadvantage in the mercenary game. Hell, or any other game for that matter. But I have skills of my own! I’m a good shot. I’m cool under pressure. I should be able to get by without resorting to mods. It’d feel like falling on a crutch at this point. A crutch I shouldn’t need.”
rows.translation: 佣兵重重吐出一口气，揉起了太阳穴。“我知道这会让我在佣兵这一行处于劣势。见鬼，其实做任何事都一样。但我有自己的本事！我枪法准，压力之下也能保持冷静。我理应能不靠改造过活。现在再用改造，就像拄上了拐杖。一根我本不该需要的拐杖。”
rows.raw: "\n\nThe mercenary exhales heavily, now rubbing at her temples. “I know that puts me at a disadvantage in the mercenary game. Hell, or any other game for that matter. But I have skills of my own! I’m a good shot. I’m cool under pressure. I should be able to get by without resorting to mods. It’d feel like falling on a crutch at this point. A crutch I shouldn’t need.”"

joinAfter.expression: pc.isBimbo() ? "“Not even a little? Not just a teensy weensy bit?”" : "“Not even a little?”"

rows.original: “Not even a little? Not just a teensy weensy bit?”
rows.translation: “一点都没有？连一丁丁丁点都没有？”
rows.raw: "“Not even a little? Not just a teensy weensy bit?”"

rows.original: “Not even a little?”
rows.translation: “一点都没有？”
rows.raw: "“Not even a little?”"

rows.original: You can’t help but to probe her a little further. “Or anything purely cosmetic?”
rows.translation: 你忍不住又追问了一句。“纯粹改变外观的也不行？”
rows.raw: " You can’t help but to probe her a little further. “Or anything purely cosmetic?”"

rows.original: “Not even a little.” She stands firm. “And nothing cosmetic, either. It’s the same principle for me; I know that if I woke up one day, looked in the mirror, and saw someone else looking back at me, it’d freak me right the fuck out. I don’t think I could handle not being able to recognize my own reflection. Maybe I don’t always like my appearance, but the important thing is that it’s mine, and I don’t want to change it.”
rows.translation: “一点也不行。”她态度坚决。“改变外观的也不行。对我来说道理是一样的；我知道，如果某天醒来照镜子，却看到另一个人回望着我，我他妈肯定会吓坏。我觉得自己承受不了连镜中的自己都认不出来。也许我并不总喜欢自己的长相，但重要的是，那是我的，而我不想改变它。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Not even a little.” She stands firm. “And nothing cosmetic, either. It’s the same principle for me; I know that if I woke up one day, looked in the mirror, and saw someone else looking back at me, it’d freak me right the fuck out. I don’t think I could handle not being able to recognize my own reflection. Maybe I don’t always like my appearance, but the important thing is that it’s mine, and I don’t want to change it.”"

rows.original: “Awww, but you’re so pretty already!” you gush, because she’s actually super cute and you’ve just got to tell her that. The response elicits a blush, which is also pretty adorable.
rows.translation: “噢，可你已经这么漂亮了！”你热情地说道，因为她确实超级可爱，你实在忍不住想告诉她。这个回答让她红了脸，而那模样同样可爱极了。
rows.raw: "\n\n“Awww, but you’re so pretty already!” you gush, because she’s actually super cute and you’ve just got to tell her that. The response elicits a blush, which is also pretty adorable."

rows.original: “Nonsense, you look fine!” you reassure her, which manages to get her to smile despite herself.
rows.translation: “胡说，你看起来挺好的！”你安慰她，让她不由自主地露出了笑容。
rows.raw: "\n\n“Nonsense, you look fine!” you reassure her, which manages to get her to smile despite herself."

rows.original: “I don’t know, I personally like what I see plenty,” you say with a wolfish smile. Your lackadaisy flirting isn’t taken too seriously, but it still elicits a smile from the woman.
rows.translation: “不知道啊，反正我觉得眼前这样就很养眼，”你带着狼一般的笑容说道。你漫不经心的调情没被她太当真，但仍让她露出了笑容。
rows.raw: "\n\n“I don’t know, I personally like what I see plenty,” you say with a wolfish smile. Your lackadaisy flirting isn’t taken too seriously, but it still elicits a smile from the woman."

rows.original: “Well, that’s dumb,” you retort. “There’s this little process called ‘aging’. It’ll change your face whether you like it or not.” Your response earns a defeated sigh. You know you’re not wrong.
rows.translation: “这也太蠢了，”你反驳道。“有个小过程叫‘衰老’。不管你愿不愿意，它都会改变你的脸。”你的回答换来一声无奈的叹息。你知道自己没说错。
rows.raw: "\n\n“Well, that’s dumb,” you retort. “There’s this little process called ‘aging’. It’ll change your face whether you like it or not.” Your response earns a defeated sigh. You know you’re not wrong."

rows.original: Nevertheless, Evening continues.
rows.translation: 尽管如此，伊芙宁还是继续说了下去。
rows.raw: " Nevertheless, Evening continues."

rows.original: “Even so, I’ve lived for so long looking like this that I feel like if I altered my appearance at all, it’d still be like changing my identity in some way. And I want to stay myself for as long as I possibly can, natural aging be damned.”
rows.translation: “即便如此，我顶着这副模样活了太久，总觉得只要稍微改变外表，就像是在某种程度上改变自己的身份。我想尽可能久地保持自我，管他自然衰老不衰老。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Even so, I’ve lived for so long looking like this that I feel like if I altered my appearance at all, it’d still be like changing my identity in some way. And I want to stay myself for as long as I possibly can, natural aging be damned.”"

rows.original: With a weary exhale, Evening finishes off her glass, orders another drink of cream liquor. “Principles aside,” the Terran postulates, “there’s plenty of practical issues too. What about the money? What about Taint? What about cooking your DNA like a metal spoon in a microwave and irreversibly fucking your body beyond repair? I do not have the credits or time to deal with that kind of shit.”
rows.translation: 伊芙宁疲惫地呼出一口气，喝光杯中酒，又点了一杯奶油利口酒。“先不谈原则，”这位地球人推论道，“现实问题也多得很。钱怎么办？污染度怎么办？要是像把金属勺扔进微波炉一样煮坏了你的DNA，把身体不可逆转地毁得再也修不好，又怎么办？我才没有信用点或时间去应付这种破事。”
rows.raw: "\n\nWith a weary exhale, Evening finishes off her glass, orders another drink of cream liquor. “Principles aside,” the Terran postulates, “there’s plenty of practical issues too. What about the money? What about Taint? What about cooking your DNA like a metal spoon in a microwave and irreversibly fucking your body beyond repair? I do not have the credits or time to deal with that kind of shit.”"

rows.original: “So you’re afraid?” you ask.
rows.translation: “所以你是在害怕？”你问道。
rows.raw: "\n\n“So you’re afraid?” you ask."

rows.original: “I prefer the term ‘risk averse’, thank you very much.” She shoots you a grim smile. “And the risk doesn’t just lie with the mod. What if there’s something wrong with you? You could try the tiniest transformative in the world and... I don’t know, maybe you turn out to be allergic. Maybe it interacts badly with something in your blood and leaves you crippled somehow.”
rows.translation: “我更喜欢‘规避风险’这个说法，多谢。”她朝你挤出一个冷峻的笑容。“而且风险不只来自改造品。万一有问题的是你呢？你可能只是试了世上作用最轻微的转化物，然后...我不知道，也许结果发现自己过敏。也许它和你血液里的某种东西发生不良反应，害你落下残疾。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“I prefer the term ‘risk averse’, thank you very much.” She shoots you a grim smile. “And the risk doesn’t just lie with the mod. What if there’s something wrong with you? You could try the tiniest transformative in the world and... I don’t know, maybe you turn out to be allergic. Maybe it interacts badly with something in your blood and leaves you crippled somehow.”"

rows.original: “Even worse, maybe it does nothing wrong, but you find yourself wanting to try something else, something bigger, because you’re not satisfied with it. As soon as you open yourself up to the possibility of change, it can make you think you’re never good enough. You think your teeth are too dull. You think your breasts are too small. You want to grow a tail, or wings, or extra limbs. You think if you don’t change yourself, you won’t be able to keep up with everyone else that does. And you think that using a mod will solve your problems, when all you do is replace them with new ones. So you keep going, constantly replacing your problems and your body parts and adding new ones until you’re an entirely other person.”
rows.translation: “更糟的是，也许它没造成任何问题，可你会因为不满意而想试别的，试效果更强的东西。一旦你向改变的可能性敞开大门，它就会让你觉得自己永远不够好。你觉得牙齿太钝，觉得乳房太小，想长出尾巴、翅膀或更多肢体。你觉得自己若不改变，就追不上其他改变了的人。你还以为使用改造品能解决问题，实际上却只是用新问题替换旧问题。于是你不断继续，不断替换自己的问题和身体部位，又不断增添新的，直到彻底变成另一个人。”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Even worse, maybe it does nothing wrong, but you find yourself wanting to try something else, something bigger, because you’re not satisfied with it. As soon as you open yourself up to the possibility of change, it can make you think you’re never good enough. You think your teeth are too dull. You think your breasts are too small. You want to grow a tail, or wings, or extra limbs. You think if you don’t change yourself, you won’t be able to keep up with everyone else that does. And you think that using a mod will solve your problems, when all you do is replace them with new ones. So you keep going, constantly replacing your problems and your body parts and adding new ones until you’re an entirely other person.”"

rows.original: “It’s a slippery slope. Maybe other people don’t think so... and maybe they think they can bite off plenty with room to chew. But I’ve seen many, and I mean way too many people get addicted to mods. And then it ruins their lives; it sinks them into debt, and it destroys their relationships with the people they love.” Her expression darkens, eyes piercing right through you.
rows.translation: “这是一条越滑越深的斜坡。也许别人不这么想...也许他们觉得自己胃口再大也吃得消。但我见过很多人，我是说，多得多的人对改造上瘾。然后改造毁掉了他们的生活；让他们债台高筑，也摧毁了他们与所爱之人的关系。”她神色阴沉下来，目光仿佛将你刺穿。
rows.raw: "\n\n“It’s a slippery slope. Maybe other people don’t think so... and maybe they think they can bite off plenty with room to chew. But I’ve seen many, and I mean way too many people get addicted to mods. And then it ruins their lives; it sinks them into debt, and it destroys their relationships with the people they love.” Her expression darkens, eyes piercing right through you."

rows.original: Her earlier remarks about you looking different start to come back to haunt you.
rows.translation: 她先前那些说你看起来不一样的话开始在你脑海里阴魂不散。
rows.raw: " Her earlier remarks about you looking different start to come back to haunt you."

rows.original: “Call me paranoid, but I’d rather not take the risk.”
rows.translation: “你可以说我多疑，但我宁愿不冒这个险。”
rows.raw: " “Call me paranoid, but I’d rather not take the risk.”"

rows.original: Considering what Evening told you about her mother, her reaction makes a lot of sense. At the very least you’re pretty sure you don’t have to worry about the same thing happening to you, thanks to the nanobots your father left you.
rows.translation: 考虑到伊芙宁告诉你的母亲经历，她会有这种反应很合理。至少你相当确定，得益于父亲留给你的纳米机器人，你不必担心同样的事情发生在自己身上。
rows.raw: "\n\nConsidering what Evening told you about her mother, her reaction makes a lot of sense. At the very least you’re pretty sure you don’t have to worry about the same thing happening to you, thanks to the nanobots your father left you."

rows.original: With an impassioned speech
rows.translation: 在一番慷慨激昂的演说后
rows.raw: "\n\nWith an impassioned speech"

rows.original: With a laundry list of issues
rows.translation: 在列举了一长串问题后
rows.raw: "\n\nWith a laundry list of issues"

rows.original: With a long-winded rant
rows.translation: 在一通长篇大论后
rows.raw: "\n\nWith a long-winded rant"

rows.original: like that, you can’t help but feel like Evening is hiding something. Mod addiction is a real thing, but
rows.translation: 听她这么说，你不禁觉得伊芙宁隐瞒了什么。改造上瘾确实存在，但
rows.raw: " like that, you can’t help but feel like Evening is hiding something. Mod addiction is a real thing, but "

joinAfter.expression:
pc.IQ() >= 75
                            ? "the chances of developing an addiction are statistically very small."
                            : "there can’t possibly be that many people who actually suffer from it."

rows.original: the chances of developing an addiction are statistically very small.
rows.translation: 从统计数据来看，产生成瘾的概率非常小。
rows.raw: "the chances of developing an addiction are statistically very small."

rows.original: there can’t possibly be that many people who actually suffer from it.
rows.translation: 真正受其折磨的人不可能有那么多。
rows.raw: "there can’t possibly be that many people who actually suffer from it."

rows.original: She doesn’t seem to be lying, but she definitely isn’t giving you the whole story either. Maybe on a later day, she’ll be willing to tell you more.
rows.translation: 她看起来不像在撒谎，但显然也没把事情全告诉你。也许改天她会愿意透露更多。
rows.raw: " She doesn’t seem to be lying, but she definitely isn’t giving you the whole story either. Maybe on a later day, she’ll be willing to tell you more."

rows.original: Still... her story strikes a chord with you. “I get how you feel,” you tell her. “My dad died recently because of transformation-induced taint.
rows.translation: 不过...她的故事触动了你的心弦。“我理解你的感受，”你告诉她。“我父亲最近因为转化诱发的腐化去世了。
rows.raw: "\n\nStill... her story strikes a chord with you. “I get how you feel,” you tell her. “My dad died recently because of transformation-induced taint."

rows.original: It was a huge bummer, trust me.”
rows.translation: 相信我，那实在令人难受。”
rows.raw: " It was a huge bummer, trust me.”"

rows.original: I miss him a lot.” A hard lump forms in your throat, the sensation pricking your eyes with tears. With the Planet Rush and your search for the probes, you never stopped to think about how damn sad thinking about it would be. Your dad is dead.
rows.translation: 我非常想念他。”你的喉咙哽住，眼眶也被刺痛般涌出泪水。在投身大开拓时代、寻找探针的过程中，你从未停下来想过，回忆这件事竟会如此悲伤。你的父亲已经去世了。
rows.raw: " I miss him a lot.” A hard lump forms in your throat, the sensation pricking your eyes with tears. With the Planet Rush and your search for the probes, you never stopped to think about how damn sad thinking about it would be. Your dad is dead."

rows.original: He went way overboard and it bit him in the ass. I wish every day that it hadn’t.” A lump forms in your throat at the thought. With the Planet Rush and your search for the probes, you never stopped to think about how damn sad thinking about it would be. Your dad is dead.
rows.translation: 他做得太过火，最后反噬了自己。我每天都希望那一切没有发生。”一想到这件事，你的喉咙便哽住了。忙于行星开拓潮和寻找探针期间，你从未停下来想过，认真回想这一切会有多么令人悲伤。你的父亲已经死了。
rows.raw: " He went way overboard and it bit him in the ass. I wish every day that it hadn’t.” A lump forms in your throat at the thought. With the Planet Rush and your search for the probes, you never stopped to think about how damn sad thinking about it would be. Your dad is dead."

rows.original: He lived over two hundred years, but I only got to share twenty of them with him.” A lump forms in your throat, but you also find yourself clenching your fist at the thought. With the Planet Rush and your search for the probes, you never stopped to think about how damn unfair it was. Victor got to have a long life. Why did you only get to be there for so little of it?
rows.translation: 他活了两百多年，可我只与他共度了其中二十年。”你的喉咙一阵发紧，想到这里又不禁攥紧拳头。忙于行星开拓潮和寻找探针期间，你从未停下来想过，这一切究竟有多么不公平。维克托拥有漫长的一生。为什么你只能陪伴他那么短的时间？
rows.raw: " He lived over two hundred years, but I only got to share twenty of them with him.” A lump forms in your throat, but you also find yourself clenching your fist at the thought. With the Planet Rush and your search for the probes, you never stopped to think about how damn unfair it was. Victor got to have a long life. Why did you only get to be there for so little of it?"

rows.original: “Oh, [pc.name]...” Evening’s face crumples in sympathy. She suddenly lurches forward and wraps her arms around you in a tight hug.
rows.translation: “哦，[pc.name]...”伊芙宁的脸因同情而垮了下来。她突然扑上前，伸出双臂紧紧抱住你。
rows.raw: "\n\n“Oh, [pc.name]...” Evening’s face crumples in sympathy. She suddenly lurches forward and wraps her arms around you in a tight hug."

rows.original: You return it warmly, pulling her close.
rows.translation: 你热情地回抱她，把她搂近。
rows.raw: " You return it warmly, pulling her close."

rows.original: After getting over the initial shock, you eventually return it.
rows.translation: 熬过最初的震惊后，你最终回抱了她。
rows.raw: " After getting over the initial shock, you eventually return it."

rows.original: It catches you off guard, but you don’t push her off.
rows.translation: 这让你措手不及，但你没有把她推开。
rows.raw: " It catches you off guard, but you don’t push her off."

rows.original: “I’m sorry about your dad. I didn’t know you went through something like that. I know what it’s like when someone... leaves you like that. It hurts a lot. I promise it gets better in time. Maybe not quickly, but it does.”
rows.translation: “你父亲的事，我很遗憾。我不知道你经历过这种事。我明白有人像那样...离开你时是什么感受。真的很痛苦。我保证，时间久了会好起来。也许不会很快，但一定会的。”
rows.raw: " “I’m sorry about your dad. I didn’t know you went through something like that. I know what it’s like when someone... leaves you like that. It hurts a lot. I promise it gets better in time. Maybe not quickly, but it does.” "

rows.original: When she pulls away, she looks like she’s about to say something else, only to change her mind. Instead, the woman musters up a reassuring smile and gives you a hearty slap on the shoulder. “Let’s talk about something less depressing, shall we?”
rows.translation: 她松开你时，看起来像还想说些什么，却又改变了主意。最后，她挤出一个安慰的笑容，用力拍了拍你的肩膀。“我们聊点没这么压抑的，好吗？”
rows.raw: "\n\nWhen she pulls away, she looks like she’s about to say something else, only to change her mind. Instead, the woman musters up a reassuring smile and gives you a hearty slap on the shoulder. “Let’s talk about something less depressing, shall we?”"

rows.original: You’re met with a nod. “That is an accurate statement about me, yes. In fact, I’d call it one of my defining characteristics,” the part-time mercenary confirms. She says it as a point of pride; no amount of shame seems to be getting between her and her love of firearms.
rows.translation: 她点了点头。“对，这么说我很准确。事实上，我会把它称作自己最鲜明的特征之一，”这位兼职佣兵确认道。她说得颇为自豪；无论怎样的羞耻心，都挡不住她对枪械的热爱。

rows.translation: “你会不会，就是说...”你模仿古董西部片里的动作，用手比画着转枪。“会玩什么花样吗？比如转枪、抛起来再接住，或者从两腿之间开枪？”

rows.original: , I’ll have you know that guns are not toys, they are weapons. They are delicate instruments of destruction and deserve to be treated as such.” And then, as she claps a hand on your shoulder: “So you bet your ass I can.”
rows.translation: ，我要告诉你，枪不是玩具，而是武器。它们是精密的毁灭工具，理应受到相应的对待。”说完，她一只手拍上你的肩膀：“所以我当然他妈的会。”

rows.original: You grin as you realize that she was just messing with you. “Wanna prove it?”
rows.translation: 你意识到她只是在逗你，于是咧嘴一笑。“想证明一下吗？”
rows.raw: "\n\nYou grin as you realize that she was just messing with you. “Wanna prove it?”"

rows.original: “Well, I would,” the mercenary laments, before subtly gesturing in Karrah’s direction and saying, “but I don’t think our fine proprietors would appreciate me waving around any weapons, no matter how discreetly. Let’s say we take a rain check?”
rows.translation: “唔，我倒是想，”这名佣兵惋惜道，随后不动声色地朝卡拉的方向示意，接着说，“不过我觉得这里出色的店主不会喜欢我挥舞任何武器，不管动作多隐蔽。改天再演示，怎么样？”
rows.raw: "\n\n“Well, I would,” the mercenary laments, before subtly gesturing in Karrah’s direction and saying, “but I don’t think our fine proprietors would appreciate me waving around any weapons, no matter how discreetly. Let’s say we take a rain check?”"

rows.original: She has a point. “Fair enough,” you say with a nod. You’ll have to remember this for if you ever bump into her outside of The Crash Landing.
rows.translation: 她说得有道理。“也对。”你点头说道。如果以后在坠落点以外的地方碰到她，你得记住这件事。
rows.raw: "\n\nShe has a point. “Fair enough,” you say with a nod. You’ll have to remember this for if you ever bump into her outside of The Crash Landing."
